definition_zh: 口袋；衣袋；一小块地区；袖珍的；把…据为己有
definition_en: a small bag sewn into clothing for carrying things; a small area or group separated from its surroundings; a smaller than usual version of something; and to take money for oneself, often dishonestly
core_image: 外套内侧缝着一只小布袋，手一探就摸到几枚硬币
scene: 外套挂在门后，手伸进内侧的布兜，摸到几枚温热的硬币。He slid the coins back into his coat pocket and shut the door.
sceneCN: 这里 pocket 是「口袋、衣袋」（第 1 个义项：缝在衣服上、开口朝上的小布袋）；句意为他把硬币塞回外套口袋，关上了门。图中可辨识物件：门后的外套、内侧布兜、硬币。

collocations.zh: 在某人的口袋里；受某人控制

derivatives.zh: 由 pocket 加表示「一…之量」的后缀 -ful 构成，义为「一袋之量」
由 pocket 与 book 复合而成，义为「钱包；袖珍手册」
由 pocket 与 knife 复合而成，义为「随身小折刀」

senses.title: A small bag sewn into clothing
senses.definition: a small bag or piece of cloth sewn into clothing, open at the top, used for carrying small objects
senses.definitionCN: 缝在衣服上、上端开口、用来装小物件的小布袋或布片
senses.example: He kept the key in his trouser pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 他把钥匙放在裤子口袋里。
senses.why: The word began as a name for any small bag, and when such a bag was stitched inside a garment it stopped being carried and became part of what you wear.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初泛指小袋子；当这种小袋子被缝进衣服里面，它就不再被提在手上，而成了穿着之物的一部分。

senses.title: A small area or group set apart
senses.definition: a small area that differs from what surrounds it, or a small separate group of people or things
senses.definitionCN: 与周围环境不同的一小块地方，或与外界分开的一小群人、一小批事物
senses.example: A pocket of resistance held out in the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 山间还有一小股抵抗力量在坚持。
senses.why: A pocket holds things apart from the open space around them, and the same containment is pictured on a map: a small patch or group enclosed by something larger.
senses.whyCN: 口袋把东西与周围的空间隔开，同样的「围住」被搬到了地图上：被更大范围包住的一小块地方或一小群人。

senses.title: Small enough to carry in a pocket
senses.definition: small enough to be carried in a pocket, or made in a smaller size than the usual one
senses.definitionCN: 小得可以装进口袋，或做得比通常尺寸更小的
senses.example: She carried a pocket dictionary to class.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着一本袖珍词典去上课。
senses.why: Once a pocket sets the measure of what can be carried on the body, anything built to that measure earns the word as an adjective: a pocket edition fits where a full one cannot.
senses.whyCN: 口袋一旦成为「能随身带走」的尺度，任何按这个尺度做出来的东西就获得了这个形容词：袖珍版放得进大版本放不进的地方。

senses.title: To take money for oneself
senses.definition: to take or keep money that belongs to another person, especially in a quiet or dishonest way
senses.definitionCN: 把属于别人的钱拿走或留下，尤指悄悄地、不诚实地做
senses.example: The clerk pocketed part of the takings.
senses.exampleCN: 那名职员把一部分营业收入装进了自己腰包。
senses.why: To put something in your pocket is to make it disappear from view and keep it, so the physical act becomes a metaphor for quietly keeping money that was never yours.
senses.whyCN: 把东西放进自己口袋，就是让它从眼前消失并留下，于是这个身体动作变成了暗地里留下不属于自己的钱的比喻。

intro.en: Pocket came into English from Anglo-Norman French for a small bag; the older source of that bag word is usually traced to Germanic, though the exact form is uncertain.
intro.cn: pocket 从盎格鲁-诺曼法语中表示小袋的词进入英语；这个小袋词更早的来源一般认为属日耳曼语族，但确切形式不确定。

items.en: A Germanic word for a bag or pouch is usually thought to lie behind the French forms, but no single source form can be reconstructed with confidence.
items.cn: 一般认为法语中的这些形式背后有一个日耳曼语表示袋子、荷包的词，但无法有把握地重构出唯一源头形式，来源不确定。

items.en: Old French poche named a bag or pouch, a soft container gathered at the top rather than a stiff box.
items.cn: 古法语 poche 指袋子、荷包，是一种上端收拢的软容器，而不是硬邦邦的盒子。

items.en: Anglo-Norman added the diminutive ending -et, so poket named a little bag, the size of a handful.
items.cn: 盎格鲁-诺曼语加上指小词尾 -et，于是 poket 指一只小袋子，大小不过一把。

items.en: Middle English pocket first meant a small pouch and then the pouch sewn into a garment, which is the sense that fixed the word in everyday use.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pocket 先指小袋，后指缝在衣服上的那只袋子，正是这个义项把词固定在了日常用语里。

items.en: Modern English extends the enclosed space to pockets of resistance and pockets of woodland, uses pocket as an adjective for small sizes, and as a verb for quietly keeping money.
items.cn: 现代英语把这种围起来的小空间扩展到一小股抵抗力量、一小片林地，并用 pocket 作形容词表示小尺寸，作动词表示悄悄把钱留下。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same bag stem and two that only echo its shape; the near-meaning group gathers containers and small enclosures.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一个「袋子」词干上的词，另收两个只是形似音近的词；近义组收各类容器与小的封闭空间。

entries.definition: As much as a pocket can hold, formed with the suffix -ful.
entries.definitionCN: 一袋之量；由 pocket 加后缀 -ful 构成。

entries.definition: A wallet or a small notebook, a compound whose first element is pocket.
entries.definitionCN: 钱包或袖珍笔记本；由 pocket 与 book 复合而成。

entries.definition: A small parcel or container; it shares the diminutive ending -et but is built on pack, so the two are close in form only.
entries.definitionCN: 小包、小盒；共享指小词尾 -et，却建立在 pack 之上，只是形式相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A figure moved by strings or by a hand; the similarity is in sound and spelling, and the origin is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 用线或手操纵的人偶；只是读音与拼写相近，来源无关。

entries.definition: A small soft bag, often worn at the waist or forming part of an animal's body.
entries.definitionCN: 柔软的小袋子，常系在腰间，或为动物身体的一部分。

entries.definition: A container of soft material with an opening at the top, used for carrying things.
entries.definitionCN: 用软材料制成、上端开口、用来装东西的容器。

entries.definition: A small flat case for carrying money, cards and papers.
entries.definitionCN: 装钱、卡片与票据的小扁盒。

entries.definition: One of the separate sections into which a space is divided.
entries.definitionCN: 把一处空间分隔开来的其中一格。

normalIntro.en: A French word for a small bag sits at the centre, and the family keeps the picture of something enclosed, held close, and kept out of sight.
normalIntro.cn: 核心是一个法语中表示小袋的词，整族词都保留着「被围住、贴身收着、不让人看见」的画面。

normal.en: Old French poche was a bag, and the ending -et made it a little bag, which is exactly what a pocket is.
normal.cn: 古法语 poche 是袋子，词尾 -et 把它变成小袋子，而口袋正是一只小袋子。

normal.en: The oldest English sense is a pouch carried in the hand; only later was it sewn into clothing and worn.
normal.cn: 英语里最古老的义项是提在手上的小袋，后来它才被缝进衣服穿在身上。

normal.en: Pocket money and pocket-sized both use the same measure: what fits in a pocket, or what is small enough to be spent from one.
normal.cn: pocket money 与 pocket-sized 用的是同一个尺度：装得进口袋，或小得能从口袋里掏出来。

normal.en: Pickpocket names the person and the act together, because the thief reaches for the pocket rather than the bag.
normal.cn: pickpocket 把人跟动作合在一起，因为下手的地方是口袋，不是提包。

normal.en: The verb is regular, and to pocket money is simply to make it vanish into that enclosed space.
normal.cn: 动词变化规则；to pocket money 就是让钱消失进那个围起来的地方。

abstract.en: A pocket is a room in a garment: small, private, and closed to everyone else.
abstract.cn: 口袋是衣服里的一间小屋：狭小、私密，对旁人关着门。

abstract.en: A pocket of resistance is the same shape drawn on a map, a small space held inside a larger one.
abstract.cn: 一小股抵抗力量就是把这个形状画在地图上：被更大范围围住的一小块空间。

abstract.en: To pocket what is not yours is to shrink the world until only your own hand remains in it.
abstract.cn: 把不属于自己的东西据为己有，就是把世界缩小到只剩自己的一只手。

examples.en: He kept the key in his trouser pocket.
examples.cn: 他把钥匙放在裤子口袋里。

examples.en: She carried a pocket dictionary to class.
examples.cn: 她带着一本袖珍词典去上课。

examples.en: The clerk pocketed part of the takings.
examples.cn: 那名职员把一部分营业收入装进了自己腰包。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕磕它」——口袋里装的都是怕磕碰的小东西，手总护着；记住 pocket 是口袋。

root: pocket 来自盎格鲁-诺曼法语 poket，是古法语 poche（袋子）加指小词尾 -et 而成的小袋；poche 更早的来源一般认为属日耳曼语族，但确切形式不确定，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a small bag held close to the body; the senses run from the sewn-in pocket, to an enclosed patch on a map, to the size that fits inside one, and finally to the act of quietly keeping what goes in.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一只贴身的小袋子；义项从缝进衣服的口袋，走到地图上被围住的一小块，再到装得进去的尺寸，最后落到悄悄留下放进来的东西这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small cloth bag stitched inside a coat, a hand closing around warm coins.
core.cn: 核心意象：外套内侧缝着的小布袋，手合拢握住几枚温热的硬币。

branches.en: a hand slipping into a coat pocket
branches.cn: 手伸进外套口袋

branches.en: a coin moving from the till into a sleeve
branches.cn: 硬币从钱箱进了袖子

branches.en: a small stand of trees on a bare hill
branches.cn: 光秃山坡上一小片树林

branches.en: a small band holding out in the hills
branches.cn: 山间坚持的一小股人马

branches.en: a dictionary small enough to fit a coat
branches.cn: 小得能塞进外套的词典

intro.en: The word is a French diminutive of a bag noun, and English builds its compounds and its verb from that same enclosed-space picture.
intro.cn: 这个词是法语中「袋子」一词的指小形式，英语又从这个「围起来的小空间」画面造出复合词与动词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; it reached English through French from a bag word usually traced to Germanic, so no Latin entry is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它经法语进入英语，源头一般认为属于日耳曼语族中表示袋子的词，因此不列拉丁条目。

items.meaning: as much as a pocket holds

definition_zh: 诗；诗歌；诗一般的事物
definition_en: a piece of writing arranged in lines, usually with rhythm and often with rhyme, that expresses feeling or thought; the form such works belong to; and something so beautiful or moving that it seems like one
core_image: 一页纸上短行错落，行末的字轻轻碰到一起
scene: 夜里灯下摊着一本薄薄的诗集，行与行之间留出大片空白。She read the poem twice before she understood why it ended with a question.
sceneCN: 这里 poem 是「诗、诗歌」（第 1 个义项：分行排列、讲究节奏的单篇作品）；句意为她读了两遍，才明白这首诗为什么以一个问句收尾。图中可辨识物件：诗集、台灯、行间的大片留白。

derivatives.zh: 与 poem 同出希腊语 poiein（制作），经拉丁语 poeta 进入英语，义为「诗人」
由 poet 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「诗的；富有诗意的」
与 poem 同源，经古法语 poeterie 进入英语，义为「诗歌（总称）；诗艺」

senses.title: A piece of writing in lines
senses.definition: a piece of writing arranged in short lines, usually with rhythm and often with rhyme, that expresses feeling or thought
senses.definitionCN: 分行排列、通常讲究节奏并常有押韵、用来表达情感或想法的作品
senses.example: He copied the poem into the back of his notebook.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那首诗抄在笔记本的末页。
senses.why: Greek poiein meant to make, and a poem was first simply a thing made; what made it special was the shaping of words into measured lines rather than any subject matter.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 poiein 意为制作，诗最初只是「做出来的东西」；使它特别的不是题材，而是把词语排成有节度的行。

senses.title: Verse writing as a form
senses.definition: the form of writing that such works belong to, considered as a genre beside prose and drama
senses.definitionCN: 这类作品所属的写作形式，与散文、戏剧并列的一种文体
senses.example: The poem as a form survived the rise of the novel.
senses.exampleCN: 诗歌作为一种文体，在小说兴起之后依然存续。
senses.why: Once a single made thing is recognised, the whole kind it belongs to can be named by the same word, so poem can stand for the form itself, not just one copy of it.
senses.whyCN: 单件「做出来的东西」一旦被认出来，它所属的整类也能用同一个词来指，于是 poem 能指这种文体本身，而不只是其中一件。

senses.title: Something as beautiful as a poem
senses.titleCN: 诗一般的事物；极美之物
senses.definition: something so beautiful, moving or finely made that it seems like a poem
senses.definitionCN: 美、动人或者做得精巧到像诗一样的事物
senses.example: The garden after rain was a poem in green and silver.
senses.exampleCN: 雨后的园子是一首由绿与银写成的诗。
senses.why: Because a poem is the most compressed and ordered use of language, any scene with the same order and economy can be praised by calling it a poem.
senses.whyCN: 诗是语言最凝练、最有秩序的一种用法，因此任何具备同样秩序与节制的景象，都可以被称作一首诗来称赞。

intro.en: Poem goes back to a Greek verb meaning to make; the thing made became a work in verse, and the word travelled through Latin and French into English.
intro.cn: poem 上溯到一个意为「制作」的希腊语动词；被做出来的东西后来指韵文作品，这个词再经拉丁语与法语进入英语。

items.en: Greek poiein meant to make, to produce or to compose, and it could be used of any craft, not only of writing.
items.cn: 希腊语 poiein 意为制作、产出、创作，可用于任何手艺，并不限于写作。

items.en: The noun poiema named a thing made, a piece of work, and in time it narrowed to a work composed in verse.
items.cn: 名词 poiema 指做出来的东西、一件作品，后来收窄为用韵文写成的作品。

items.en: Latin borrowed poiema as poema, keeping the sense of a poem or a piece of verse, and passed it to the learned writers of Europe.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 poiema 借作 poema，保留了诗、韵文作品的意思，并把它传给欧洲的文人。

items.en: Old French poeme carried the word into ordinary literary use, and English took it over in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 poeme 把这个词带入普通的文学用语，英语在十六世纪把它借了过来。

items.en: Modern English keeps poem for a single work, poetry for the art as a whole, and poet for the maker, all from the same Greek verb.
items.cn: 现代英语用 poem 指单篇作品，用 poetry 指这门艺术整体，用 poet 指创作者，三者同出一个希腊语动词。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Greek verb for making and the family it produced; the near-meaning group gathers kinds of verse and the parts of verse craft.
note.cn: 形近组沿希腊语表示「制作」的动词及其词族展开；近义组收各种诗体与作诗手法。

entries.definition: A person who writes poems; the Greek maker became the maker of verse.
entries.definitionCN: 写诗的人；希腊语里「制作的人」成了作诗的人。

entries.definition: Poems considered as a whole, or the art of writing them.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体的诗歌，或写诗这门艺术。

entries.definition: Relating to poems, or having the beauty and compression of verse.
entries.definitionCN: 与诗有关的，或具有诗的美的凝练。

entries.definition: The study or theory of poetry as a craft.
entries.definitionCN: 把诗当作一门手艺来研究的学问或理论。

entries.definition: Writing arranged in lines with rhythm, or one line of such writing.
entries.definitionCN: 按节奏分行排列的文字，或其中的一行。

entries.definition: A short poem expressing personal feeling, or the words of a song.
entries.definitionCN: 表达个人情感的短诗，或歌词。

entries.definition: A poem of fourteen lines with a fixed pattern of rhyme.
entries.definitionCN: 十四行、押韵格式固定的诗。

entries.definition: A matching of word endings in sound, or a short poem that uses it.
entries.definitionCN: 词尾读音相合，或使用这种相合的小诗。

normalIntro.en: The whole family grows from one Greek verb for making, so poem, poet and poetry all carry the idea of something crafted rather than merely spoken.
normalIntro.cn: 整族词都从一个希腊语表示「制作」的动词长出来，所以 poem、poet、poetry 都带着「被精心做出来」而不是随口说出的意味。

normal.en: Greek poiein means to make, so a poem is literally something made, like a table or a pot.
normal.cn: 希腊语 poiein 意为制作，所以 poem 字面上就是一件做出来的东西，像桌子或陶罐。

normal.en: Poiema is the thing made, and poema is its Latin form; both point to a finished piece of work rather than to inspiration.
normal.cn: poiema 是做出来的东西，poema 是它的拉丁形式；两者都指向一件完成的作品，而不是灵感。

normal.en: Poet, poem and poetry share the stem: the maker, the single work, and the art as a whole.
normal.cn: poet、poem、poetry 共用一个词干：做的人、单件作品，以及整体的艺术。

normal.en: The difference between poem and poetry is the difference between one chair and carpentry.
normal.cn: poem 与 poetry 的区别，就像一把椅子和木工这门手艺的区别。

normal.en: The word has two syllables, and the second is weak; the plural is simply poems.
normal.cn: 这个词有两个音节，第二个音节很轻；复数直接加 s 变成 poems。

abstract.en: A poem is speech that has been made to slow down, so each word can be looked at.
abstract.cn: 诗是被放慢的说话，好让每个词都值得看一眼。

abstract.en: Line breaks are breaths written down, which is why a poem looks different before it is read aloud.
abstract.cn: 分行是写下来的呼吸，所以一首诗在朗读之前，看上去就不一样。

abstract.en: Calling a garden a poem is a way of saying that order and feeling arrived at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 把园子叫作诗，是在说秩序与情感在同一刻到齐了。

examples.en: He copied the poem into the back of his notebook.
examples.cn: 他把那首诗抄在笔记本的末页。

examples.en: The poem as a form survived the rise of the novel.
examples.cn: 诗歌作为一种文体，在小说兴起之后依然存续。

examples.en: The garden after rain was a poem in green and silver.
examples.cn: 雨后的园子是一首由绿与银写成的诗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖木」——把一块木头剖开，削成一行行短句；记住 poem 是诗。

root: 希腊语 poiein（制作）造出 poiema（做出来的东西），拉丁语借作 poema（诗），经古法语 poeme 进入英语；同族有 poet（诗人）、poetry（诗歌总称）、poetic（诗的）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something deliberately made; the senses run from one crafted work in lines, to the whole form of verse writing, and then outward to anything ordered and moving enough to be called a poem.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是被有意做出来的东西；义项从一件分行写成的作品，走到韵文写作这种文体，再向外扩展到任何具备同样秩序与动人力量、足以被称作诗的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: short lines stopping well before the margin, with wide white space between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：短行在页边之前就停住，行与行之间留着大片空白。

branches.en: a line ending short of the margin
branches.cn: 行末停在页边之前

branches.en: a page with wide white gaps between the lines
branches.cn: 行间留着大片空白的书页

branches.en: slim volumes of one genre on a shelf
branches.cn: 书架上同一体裁的薄册

branches.en: a critic setting verse beside prose
branches.cn: 评论者把韵文与散文并置

branches.en: a garden shining green after rain
branches.cn: 雨后泛着绿光的花园

intro.en: The word is built on a Greek verb of making and the noun for the thing made, and the same stem gives English the maker, the art and the adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词建立在希腊语表示「制作」的动词与表示「做成之物」的名词上，同一词干又给出英语里的创作者、这门艺术与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin forms are recorded for this word: the borrowed noun poema, a poem, and poeta, the maker of one.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词有可考的拉丁形式：借入的名词 poema（诗）与 poeta（作诗的人）。

definition_zh: 要点；得分；地点；小数点；指向
definition_en: the main idea of what someone says; a unit of score; an exact place or moment; the dot in a decimal number; also to aim or show direction
core_image: 一根手指伸出去停在半空，所有人的视线顺着这条线落到墙上同一个位置
scene: 会议室里的讨论拖了很久，白板上写满潦草的字，有人忽然把笔尖按在其中一个词上。She tapped the board and made her point in one short sentence.
sceneCN: 这里 point 指「要点」（第 1 个义项：说话人最想让人记住的那一点）；句意为她敲了敲白板，用一句短话把自己的要点说清楚。图中可辨识物件：写满字的白板、按在词上的笔尖、几张转过来的脸。

derivatives.zh: 由 point 加 -ed 构成，义为「尖的；有针对性的」
由 point 加 -er 构成，义为「指示棒；提示；指针」
由 point 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无意义的；没有尖头的」
与 point 同出拉丁语 punctum，义为「准时的」，原指恰好落在某一刻

senses.title: The main idea in what is said
senses.definition: the central idea that a speaker or writer wants to be understood and remembered
senses.definitionCN: 说话人或作者最想让人理解并记住的那个中心意思
senses.example: Her point was that the plan costs far too much.
senses.exampleCN: 她的要点是这个方案花费太高。
senses.why: Latin punctum named the small mark left by a prick, and a mark is exactly what you put beside the one thing that must not be missed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 punctum 指被刺出的小痕，而人们正是用记号标出那件绝不能漏掉的事。

senses.title: A unit of score in a game or test
senses.definition: one of the units by which a game, a contest or an examination is measured
senses.definitionCN: 衡量一场比赛、一次竞赛或一场考试的计量单位
senses.example: He won the final point with a serve down the line.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一记压边线的发球拿下了最后一分。
senses.why: A score was once kept by making a small mark for each success, so the mark itself became the unit of winning.
senses.whyCN: 过去记分就是每得一分画一个小记号，于是记号本身成了计量的单位。

senses.title: A particular place or moment
senses.definition: an exact spot on a map, a body or a scale, or a particular moment in time
senses.definitionCN: 地图、身体或刻度上确切的一处，或时间上特定的某一刻
senses.example: We met at the point where the two roads meet.
senses.exampleCN: 我们约在两条路交汇的那一点见面。
senses.why: A dot fixes a position and nothing else, which is why the same noun can pin down a place on a map and a moment on a timeline.
senses.whyCN: 一个点只固定位置，别的什么也不带，所以同一个名词既能标定地图上的一处，也能标定时间轴上的一刻。

senses.title: The dot in a decimal number
senses.definition: the mark that separates the whole part of a number from its fraction
senses.definitionCN: 把一个数的整数部分与小数部分分开的记号
senses.example: The reading was three point seven metres.
senses.exampleCN: 读数是三点七米。
senses.why: Because the dot is literally a small prick on the page, the mark that splits a decimal simply inherited the name of the mark itself.
senses.whyCN: 因为那个点字面上就是纸上的一个小刺痕，分开整数与小数的记号便直接继承了「记号」这个名字。

senses.title: To aim or show direction
senses.definition: to turn a finger or an object towards something, or to show what is true or likely
senses.definitionCN: 把手指或物体转向某处，或显示出什么是真的、什么是可能发生的
senses.example: The arrow points north along the coastal path.
senses.exampleCN: 箭头指向沿海小路的北面。
senses.why: A pointed finger and a written dot do the same job, both singling out one thing among many, so the noun turned into a verb of directing attention.
senses.whyCN: 伸出的手指与纸上的点做的是同一件事，都是在众多事物里单单挑出一个，于是名词转成了引导注意的动词。

intro.en: Point comes from a Latin word for a prick and the mark it leaves; the dot is the oldest picture behind the score, the argument and the pointing finger.
intro.cn: point 出自拉丁语中表示「刺」的词以及刺出的痕迹；那个小点，就是得分、论点与指路手指背后最古老的画面。

items.en: The verb pungere meant to prick or pierce, the action of a sharp tip against a surface.
items.cn: 动词 pungere 意为刺、扎，是尖锐之物抵住表面的动作。

items.en: Its neuter past participle punctum named the tiny mark or hole left behind, and so came to mean a dot.
items.cn: 它的中性过去分词 punctum 指留下的细微痕迹或小孔，于是有了「点」的意思。

items.en: Old French point carried the dot, but also a stitch, a moment and a item in an argument.
items.cn: 古法语 point 既保留「点」，也指针脚、某一刻以及论述中的一项。

items.en: English took point first for a dot or a sharp end, then for a mark in a game and the chief item of a speech.
items.cn: 英语先以 point 指点状物或尖端，随后指比赛中的记号与讲话里的主要一项。

items.en: Modern English adds the decimal point, the pointing gesture, point of view, and dozens of fixed phrases.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上小数点、指点的动作、point of view 以及大量固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group stays on the Latin prick and its mark; the near-meaning group gathers the dot, the score, the stage and the act of aiming.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁语「刺」及其痕迹展开；近义组收点、得分、阶段与瞄准这些意思。

entries.definition: Having a sharp end, or clearly aimed at one person.
entries.definitionCN: 有尖端的；明显针对某一个人的。

entries.definition: A stick, cursor or hint that shows where to look.
entries.definitionCN: 指示棒、光标或提示。

entries.definition: Having no purpose or result at all.
entries.definitionCN: 完全没有目的或结果的。

entries.definition: Arriving exactly at the agreed time.
entries.definitionCN: 恰好在约定时刻到达的。

entries.definition: The marks such as commas and full stops used in writing.
entries.definitionCN: 书写中使用的逗号、句号等标记。

entries.definition: A small round mark.
entries.definitionCN: 小而圆的点。

entries.definition: The number of points won in a game.
entries.definitionCN: 比赛中赢得的分数。

entries.definition: A particular point in a process or development.
entries.definitionCN: 过程或发展中的某一阶段。

entries.definition: To point or direct something at a target.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物对准目标。

normalIntro.en: Everything here grows from one tiny mark made by a sharp tip, and that mark still explains the score, the argument and the finger.
normalIntro.cn: 这里的一切都长自尖端留下的一个小记号，而这个记号至今能解释得分、论点与手指。

normal.en: Pungere means to prick, and punctum is the mark a prick leaves, so every sense starts from a tiny mark.
normal.cn: pungere 意为刺，punctum 是刺出的小痕，所以每个义项都从这一个小记号出发。

normal.en: To point at something is to put an invisible dot on it, which is why the noun became a verb.
normal.cn: 指着某物，等于在它上面放一个看不见的点，名词就这样变成了动词。

normal.en: A point in a game was once a tally mark, so the score and the dot are the same mark seen twice.
normal.cn: 比赛中的一分原本就是一个记数记号，所以得分与点其实是同一个记号的两次现身。

normal.en: The decimal point is a real dot on the page, and it is the oldest physical sense surviving almost unchanged.
normal.cn: 小数点是纸上真实的一点，也是几乎原封不动留存下来的最古老的实指义。

normal.en: Pointless adds -less, without a point, and the metaphor is still visible: something with nothing to aim at.
normal.cn: pointless 加 -less，意为「没有点」，比喻仍然看得见：没有可瞄准之处。

abstract.en: The same mark that measures a game also marks the one sentence worth remembering, which says how close play and argument are.
abstract.cn: 衡量比赛的记号也被用来标出那句值得记住的话，可见游戏与论辩有多近。

abstract.en: A point is a decision about where to stop: a dot chooses a place on a map the way a conclusion chooses a place in an argument.
abstract.cn: 一个点就是决定在哪里停下：圆点在地图上选定一处，正如结论在论述中选定一处。

abstract.en: When someone says you have missed the point, the image is still spatial, as if the meaning had a location you walked past.
abstract.cn: 当有人说你错过了要点，这个说法仍是空间性的，仿佛意义有一个你走过了的位置。

examples.en: Let me make one point before we vote.
examples.cn: 在投票之前，请让我说明一点。

examples.en: She has already scored twenty points this season.
examples.cn: 这个赛季她已经得了二十分。

examples.en: From this point the road climbs steeply.
examples.cn: 从这里开始，路陡然向上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖因特」——手指一剖，直直对着那一个点，不偏不倚。

root: 拉丁语 pungere（刺）→ 过去分词 punctum（刺出的点、记号）→ 古法语 point → 英语 point。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a mark made by a sharp tip; from it come the idea worth marking, the tally of a game, a fixed spot in space or time, the decimal dot and the act of aiming.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是尖端留下的一个记号；由此生出值得标记的意思、比赛的记数、时空中的定点、小数点以及瞄准的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger held out and stopped in mid-air, every eye in the room following the line to one spot on the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指伸出后停在半空，满屋的视线都顺着这条线落在墙上同一处。

branches.en: a sentence that makes a long meeting fall into place
branches.cn: 一句话让冗长的会议落到实处

branches.en: a serve landing just inside the line
branches.cn: 一记刚好落在边线内的发球

branches.en: two roads meeting at one exact spot
branches.cn: 两条路交于确切的一点

branches.en: a dot splitting a number in two
branches.cn: 一个点把数字分成两半

branches.en: a finger and a sentence both singling out one thing
branches.cn: 手指与句子都在挑出同一件事

intro.en: A Latin verb of pricking, its participle turned noun, and a French borrowing together supply the whole family of marks and aims.
intro.cn: 一个表示刺的拉丁动词、由分词转成的名词，加上一次法语借入，共同支撑起这整族关于记号与瞄准的词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 警方；警察部门；警察（人员）；维持治安；监督
definition_en: the official body that keeps public order and enforces the law, its members, and the act of keeping order in a place or process
core_image: 夜里扫过街角的蓝灯，行人自动让开一条路
scene: 深夜的街口，蓝灯在墙上扫来扫去，几个人被请到路边问话。The police closed the road after the accident and asked drivers to turn back.
sceneCN: 这里指「警方」这个机构整体（第 1 个义项：维持公共秩序的官方部门，作主语时谓语用复数）；句意为事故之后警方封了路，让司机掉头。画面里有夜色、街口和转动的蓝灯。

pos.zh: 警方；警察部门；警察（人员）

derivatives.zh: 由 police 与 man 复合而成，义为「男警察」
由 police 与 woman 复合而成，义为「女警察」
由 police 加 -ing 构成，义为「维持治安；警务工作」

senses.title: The official body that keeps public order
senses.definition: the official organization whose members keep order, prevent crime and enforce the law, grammatically treated as plural
senses.definitionCN: 负责维持秩序、预防犯罪、执行法律的官方机构，语法上按复数处理
senses.example: The police were called when the shop alarm went off.
senses.exampleCN: 商店警报响起来时，有人报了警。
senses.why: The word first named the whole administration of a city rather than its officers, so the institution itself owns the noun, and English keeps a plural verb after it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指一座城市的整套行政管理，而不是其中的警员；机构本身占住了名词，所以英语在它后面仍用复数谓语。

senses.title: The members of that body
senses.definition: the men and women who serve in that organization, counted as people rather than as an institution
senses.definitionCN: 在这个机构里任职的男男女女，按人而不是按机构来数
senses.example: Two police were standing at the gate all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 两名警察整个上午都站在门口。
senses.why: Because the noun names a body, the people inside the body are named by the same word with no plural ending, so institution and members share one form.
senses.whyCN: 名词既指一个整体，整体里的人就用同一个词来说，而且不加复数词尾，于是机构与成员共用一个形式。

senses.title: To keep order in a place
senses.definition: to keep order in an area by patrolling it and enforcing the rules there
senses.definitionCN: 在某片区域内巡逻并执行规则，从而维持秩序
senses.example: Extra officers were sent to police the square during the festival.
senses.exampleCN: 节日期间，另有警员被派去广场维持秩序。
senses.why: If the noun is the institution that keeps order, the verb is that institution set in motion over a piece of ground.
senses.whyCN: 如果名词是「维持秩序的机构」，动词就是让这个机构在一片地面上动起来。

senses.title: To control how an activity is carried out
senses.definition: to control how an agreement, system or set of rules is followed, often by a group watching its own members
senses.definitionCN: 管控某项协议、制度或规则如何被执行，常指团体自查自管
senses.example: The committee was asked to police its own spending more strictly.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会被要求更严格地管住自己的开支。
senses.why: Order has to be kept inside rules and budgets as well as on streets, so the same verb reaches from city squares into contracts and accounts.
senses.whyCN: 秩序不只在街上维持，也要在规则和预算里维持，所以这个动词从城市广场一直伸进合同与账目。

intro.en: Police goes back through French to a Latin word for the administration of a community, and its Greek ancestor is the same city word that also gave English policy.
intro.cn: police 经法语上溯到表示「共同体管理」的拉丁词，而它的希腊祖先是那个「城邦」词，英语的 policy 也出于此。

items.en: Polis meant a city and the body of citizens who belonged to it, and it supplied the whole vocabulary of civic life.
items.cn: polis 意为城邦以及属于它的公民群体，公民生活的一整套词汇都由它而来。

items.en: Politeia named citizenship and the constitution of a city, that is, the way a community was organized and governed.
items.cn: politeia 指公民身份与城邦政体，也就是一个共同体被组织和治理的方式。

items.en: Latin politia took over the sense of public administration, the running of a community as a whole.
items.cn: 拉丁语 politia 承接了「公共行政」这层意思，指把整个共同体管理起来。

items.en: Old French police meant public order and the administration that maintained it, still without any idea of a uniformed force.
items.cn: 古法语 police 指公共秩序以及维持它的行政机构，当时还没有穿制服的警队这层意思。

items.en: Modern English narrowed police to the body that keeps order and made it a plural collective; policy took the same root but drifted to a plan of action, so the two now share an origin and nothing else.
items.cn: 现代英语把 police 收窄为维持秩序的机构，并把它当作复数集体名词；policy 出于同一词根，却漂向「行动方案」，两者如今只在来源上相同，词义已不相干。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Greek city root; the near-meaning group gathers words for the people who keep order.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在希腊语「城邦」词根上的词；近义组收表示「维持秩序的人」的词。

entries.definition: A plan or course of action; it shares the Greek city root but long ago split from the meaning of public order.
entries.definitionCN: 政策；方针。与 police 同出希腊语「城邦」词根，但很早以前就从「公共秩序」这一义分叉出去了。

entries.definition: The activity of governing a country or city, from the same Greek word for the city.
entries.definitionCN: 政治；政治活动，同出那个表示城邦的希腊词。

entries.definition: The work of keeping order in an area.
entries.definitionCN: 在某一地区维持秩序的工作。

entries.definition: A male member of the police force.
entries.definitionCN: 男警察。

entries.definition: A person holding a position of authority, especially in the police.
entries.definitionCN: 担任职务、拥有权力的人，尤指警官。

entries.definition: A police officer of the lowest rank in Britain.
entries.definitionCN: 英国警衔最低的警员。

entries.definition: To move regularly through an area to watch for trouble.
entries.definitionCN: 在某一区域定时巡查以防范问题。

entries.definition: An elected law officer in a county, chiefly in the United States.
entries.definitionCN: 郡县里经选举产生的执法官，主要见于美国。

normalIntro.en: The word is the administration of a city seen from outside: first the running of a community, then the force that keeps its order.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是从外面看到的城市管理：先是共同体的运作，后来才是维持其秩序的队伍。

normal.en: The Greek root polis means city, so police and policy are cousins that grew up in the same town.
normal.cn: 希腊词根 polis 意为城邦，所以 police 与 policy 是在同一座城里长大的表亲。

normal.en: Policy took the planning side of that root and means a course of action, while police took the order side and means the force that keeps it.
normal.cn: policy 拿走这个词根的「筹划」一侧，指行动方针；police 拿走「秩序」一侧，指维持秩序的力量。

normal.en: The police takes a plural verb because the noun names a body of people, not one person.
normal.cn: the police 后面用复数谓语，因为名词指的是一群人，而不是一个人。

normal.en: Two police without a plural ending shows that the same form can name the members as well as the institution.
normal.cn: two police 不加复数词尾，说明同一个形式既指机构，也指机构里的成员。

normal.en: Police as a verb takes an object: you police a street, a match or a treaty, because order is always kept over something.
normal.cn: police 作动词要带宾语：police a street、a match、a treaty，因为秩序总是施加在某样东西上。

abstract.en: A word for city government turning into a word for a night patrol shows how abstract administration becomes visible on a street corner.
abstract.cn: 一个指城市行政的词变成指夜间巡逻的词，说明抽象的管理最终要在街角显形。

abstract.en: Police and policy split because a community needs both a plan and someone to enforce it.
abstract.cn: police 与 policy 分家，是因为一个共同体既需要方案，也需要有人去执行。

abstract.en: The plural verb is a small grammatical trace of the idea that order is kept by many hands, not one.
abstract.cn: 那个复数谓语是一点语法痕迹，记着「秩序由许多只手维持，而不是一只」。

examples.en: The police were called when the shop alarm went off.
examples.cn: 商店警报响起来时，有人报了警。

examples.en: Two police were standing at the gate all morning.
examples.cn: 两名警察整个上午都站在门口。

examples.en: Extra officers were sent to police the square during the festival.
examples.cn: 节日期间，另有警员被派去广场维持秩序。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡利斯」——街口一有动静，警车爬坡就到，办事利索，这就是 police 的警方。

root: 希腊语 polis（城邦）→ politeia（公民身份、政体）→ 拉丁语 politia（公共行政）→ 古法语 police；与 policy 同源，但 policy 走的是「施政方案」一路，词义早已分叉。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the administration of a community; it narrows into the body that keeps order, then splits into its members and into the act of keeping order.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「共同体的管理」；它收窄为维持秩序的机构，再分出机构里的成员与维持秩序这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blue light sweeping a night street while people step aside to let order pass.
core.cn: 核心意象：蓝灯扫过夜里的街道，行人自动让开一条路。

branches.en: a blue light turning at a night corner
branches.cn: 夜里拐角处转动的蓝灯

branches.en: an officer writing a name into a notebook
branches.cn: 警员把姓名记进本子

branches.en: a line of officers walking across a square
branches.cn: 一队警员横穿广场

branches.en: a committee reading a budget line by line
branches.cn: 委员会逐行核对预算

branches.en: a station desk crowded at midnight
branches.cn: 午夜挤满人的警局值班台

intro.en: A Greek word for the city, its abstract noun of citizenship, and a Latin noun of administration hold this family together, with English splitting it into the body, the members and the task.
intro.cn: 一个希腊语的「城邦」词、它表示公民身份的抽象名词，以及一个拉丁语的管理名词，共同撑起这一族；英语再把它分成机构、成员与任务。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to keep order in a place

definition_zh: 男警察；警员
definition_en: a man who is a member of the police force; a male police officer
core_image: 街角站着一名穿制服的男警，帽檐压得很正，手按在腰间的对讲机上
scene: 路口红灯坏了，车流乱成一团。A policeman stepped into the crossing and began to wave the cars through.
sceneCN: 这里 policeman 是「男警察」（第 1 个义项：警察队伍里的男性成员）；句意为一名男警察走到斑马线上，开始挥手指挥车辆通行。

senses.title: A male member of the police force
senses.definition: a man whose job is to keep order, enforce the law and help the public as a member of the police
senses.definitionCN: 以维持秩序、执行法律、帮助公众为职业的男性，属于警察队伍
senses.example: A policeman helped the old lady across the road.
senses.exampleCN: 一名男警察扶老太太过了马路。
senses.why: Police names the force as a whole, and man turns it into one person you can point at on the street.
senses.whyCN: police 指整支警察队伍，man 把它落到街上可以指着的一个具体的人身上。

senses.title: A figure of order and help
senses.definition: a person seen as the symbol of law and order, or the one you turn to when there is trouble
senses.definitionCN: 被视为法律与秩序象征的人，或出了事时大家去求助的那个人
senses.example: Every child on the street knows the policeman at the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 街上的每个孩子都认识街角那位警察。
senses.why: Because the job is standing in public with authority, the word also names the trusted figure that stands for order, not just the man in uniform.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个职业就是带着权威站在公众面前，这个词也用来指秩序本身的象征，不只是那身制服下的一个人。

intro.en: Policeman is an English compound: police, borrowed through French from a Greek word for the city and its administration, joined to man.
intro.cn: policeman 是英语复合词：police 经法语借自希腊语中表示城市及其行政的词，再与 man 复合。

items.en: Greek polis named a city or city-state, and its affairs: citizenship, administration, public order.
items.cn: 希腊语 polis 指城市或城邦，也指城市的事务：公民身份、行政、公共秩序。

items.en: From polis came politeia, the condition and organization of the citizen body, government of a city.
items.cn: 由 polis 派生出 politeia，指公民共同体的状态与组织方式，即城邦的治理。

items.en: Latin took over politeia as politia, keeping the sense of civil administration and government.
items.cn: 拉丁语吸收了 politeia 作 politia，保留公民行政与治理的含义。

items.en: Old French police meant the ordering and government of a community before it narrowed to the force that keeps order.
items.cn: 古法语 police 先指对共同体的治理与秩序安排，后来才缩小到维持秩序的那支队伍。

items.en: English compounded police with man to make policeman, one identifiable male officer of that force, with the irregular plural policemen.
items.cn: 英语把 police 与 man 复合成 policeman，指这支队伍中一名可以辨认的男性警员，复数为不规则形式 policemen。

normalIntro.en: The word is a straightforward compound, and everything in the family repeats the same two-part picture: a force, plus the man who wears it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是直白的复合词，词族里反复出现同一个两段式画面：一支队伍，加上穿着它的那个人。

normal.en: Police comes from Greek polis, the city, so a policeman is literally a man of the city's order.
normal.cn: police 来自希腊语 polis（城市），所以 policeman 字面上就是「城邦秩序之人」。

normal.en: Police + man, force + person: the compound says the whole force in one man.
normal.cn: police + man，队伍 + 人：这个复合词用一个人代表整支队伍。

normal.en: The plural is irregular: policeman becomes policemen, exactly like man becoming men.
normal.cn: 复数不规则：policeman 变 policemen，与 man 变 men 完全一致。

normal.en: The same pattern gives policewoman, fireman and postman, so once you know one you know the family.
normal.cn: 同样的构词法给出 policewoman、fireman、postman，认识一个就认识一族。

normal.en: Police is collective and takes a plural verb in British English; policeman is a single, countable person.
normal.cn: police 是集合名词，英式英语中常配复数动词；policeman 则是可数的单个人。

abstract.en: A policeman is order given a face: where he stands, the street agrees on the rules.
abstract.cn: 警察是有面孔的秩序：他站在哪里，哪条街就认同规则。

abstract.en: Calling a policeman is turning private fear into public procedure.
abstract.cn: 叫警察，就是把个人的害怕变成公开的程序。

abstract.en: The uniform erases the person and leaves only the order he carries.
abstract.cn: 制服抹掉个人，只留下他所携带的秩序。

examples.cn: 一名男警察扶老太太过了马路。

examples.cn: 巡逻的警察们在公园里找到了走失的孩子。

examples.en: If you lose your way at night, ask a policeman for directions.
examples.cn: 晚上迷路的话，向警察问路。

definition_zh: 礼貌地；客气地；委婉地；出于礼节地
definition_en: in a respectful and well-mannered way, especially when softening a refusal or following social form
core_image: 被磨圆的桌角，人从旁边走过不会被磕伤
scene: 面试结束时，年轻人起身把椅子推回原位，又向每位面试官点头道谢。She politely thanked the interviewer and closed the door quietly behind her.
sceneCN: 这里是「礼貌地、客气地」（第 1 个义项：举止合乎礼节）；句意为她客气地道了谢，轻轻带上门离开。画面里有面试桌、推回原位的椅子和点头致意的年轻人。

senses.title: In a respectful, well-mannered way
senses.definition: in a way that shows respect for other people and follows the usual rules of good manners
senses.definitionCN: 以尊重他人、符合通常礼节规范的方式
senses.example: She politely introduced herself to every guest at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她在门口客气地向每位客人做了自我介绍。
senses.why: The adjective descends from a Latin word for polished, so the adverb describes behaviour that has been smoothed down until it will not rub anyone the wrong way.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词来自拉丁语中表示「打磨过」的词，所以它形容的举止是被人磨平过的，不会硌到谁。

senses.title: In a way that softens a refusal
senses.definition: used when saying no or disagreeing in words chosen to avoid embarrassing the other person
senses.definitionCN: 在拒绝或表示不同意见时，用不使对方难堪的措辞
senses.example: He politely declined the offer and asked for more time.
senses.exampleCN: 他婉言谢绝了这个提议，请对方再给些时间。
senses.why: Once the word means smoothed manners, it is most useful exactly where friction is likely, so it clusters around refusals, complaints and disagreement.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词指的是被磨平的举止，它就最适合用在容易起摩擦的地方，于是总围着拒绝、抱怨与分歧打转。

senses.title: Out of social form rather than feeling
senses.definition: done because the situation requires courtesy, even when the feeling behind it is cold or absent
senses.definitionCN: 因为场合要求客气才这么做，背后的真实情绪可能是冷淡甚至没有
senses.example: The complaint was politely ignored for three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 那封投诉被客客气气地搁置了三个星期。
senses.why: Polish is surface work, so the adverb can mark the surface alone: the form is correct while nothing warm is happening underneath.
senses.whyCN: 打磨是表面功夫，所以这个副词可以只标记表面：形式无可挑剔，底下却没有一点热度。

intro.en: Politely is polite plus -ly, and polite goes back to a Latin verb meaning to polish, whose participle came to describe manners that had been smoothed.
intro.cn: politely 是 polite 加 -ly 构成的，而 polite 上溯到一个意为「打磨」的拉丁动词，其分词后来用来形容被磨平的举止。

items.en: Polire meant to polish or smooth a surface, and it was used of stone, wood and finished work.
items.cn: polire 意为打磨、使表面光滑，用于石头、木材与成品。

items.en: Its participle politus meant polished or refined, first of objects and then of anything carefully finished.
items.cn: 它的分词 politus 意为「被打磨过的、精致的」，先指物件，后指任何精心完成的东西。

items.en: In later learned Latin the same participle was applied to people, so a politus person was one whose manners had been smoothed.
items.cn: 在后来的学术拉丁语里，同一个分词被用到人身上，于是 politus 的人就是举止被磨平过的人。

items.en: English borrowed polite directly from Latin in the sixteenth century, and the adverb politely was formed by adding the native suffix -ly.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪直接从拉丁语借入 polite，副词 politely 则由加上本族后缀 -ly 构成。

items.en: Modern English uses politely for courteous speech, for tactful refusals, and sometimes for a courtesy that is only on the surface.
items.cn: 现代英语用 politely 表示客气的言辞、委婉的拒绝，有时也指只停留在表面的客气。

note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「打磨」一词上的形容词及其同族；近义组收表示「客气举止」的副词。

normal.cn: politely 是 polite 加 -ly，回答的是「某人如何说话、如何行事」。

normal.en: The Latin source polire means to polish, which is why politeness is pictured as a surface made smooth.
normal.cn: 拉丁语来源 polire 意为打磨，所以「礼貌」被想成被打磨光滑的表面。

normal.en: Politely decline and politely refuse are the most common patterns, because the word is needed where a no must be softened.
normal.cn: politely decline 与 politely refuse 是最常见的搭配，因为这个词正用在必须把「不」说软的地方。

normal.en: The negative is impolite, with im- before p, not unpolite in ordinary modern use.
normal.cn: 否定形式是 impolite，在 p 前用 im-，现代常用语里不说 unpolite。

normal.en: Politeness is the noun and impolitely the negative adverb, so the family covers the quality, the manner and its lack.
normal.cn: politeness 是名词，impolitely 是否定副词，这一族词因此覆盖品质、方式与两者的缺失。

abstract.en: A word borrowed from polishing suggests that manners are not Nature but work done on a rough edge.
abstract.cn: 一个从「打磨」借来的词说明：礼貌不是天性，而是在粗糙的边上做的功夫。

abstract.en: Politely can be warm or cold, because smoothness says nothing about what is underneath.
abstract.cn: politely 可以是暖的也可以是冷的，因为光滑并不说明底下是什么。

abstract.en: The most useful courtesy appears exactly where people must say no to each other.
abstract.cn: 最有用的客气，恰好出现在人们必须彼此说不的时候。

examples.en: She politely introduced herself to every guest at the door.
examples.cn: 她在门口客气地向每位客人做了自我介绍。

examples.en: He politely declined the offer and asked for more time.
examples.cn: 他婉言谢绝了这个提议，请对方再给些时间。

examples.en: The complaint was politely ignored for three weeks.
examples.cn: 那封投诉被客客气气地搁置了三个星期。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡莱特利」——把棱角磨平，把话说得体贴，人就显得客气，这就是 politely。

root: 拉丁语 polire（打磨）→ politus（被打磨过的、精致的）→ 中世纪拉丁语引申为「举止有礼的」→ 英语 polite，加 -ly 成 politely。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is smoothed behaviour; from it come the softened refusal and the courtesy that is only form.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「被磨平的举止」；由此分出委婉的拒绝，以及只停留在形式上的客气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a corner sanded round, so people can pass without being cut.
core.cn: 核心意象：被磨圆的一角，两个人擦身而过却不会互相割伤。

branches.en: a guest greeted by name at the door
branches.cn: 在门口被叫出名字问候的客人

branches.en: a head shaken gently with a smile
branches.cn: 带着笑轻轻摇头

branches.en: a letter answered with perfect but cold wording
branches.cn: 用挑不出错却冷淡的措辞回信

branches.en: a host easing a guest out without hurry
branches.cn: 主人不急不催地把客人送走

branches.en: a rejection that leaves no one embarrassed
branches.cn: 不叫任何人难堪的拒绝

intro.en: A Latin verb of polishing, its participle of refinement, and the English suffix -ly hold this adverb together, with -ness and im- building the noun and the negative.
intro.cn: 一个表示打磨的拉丁动词、它表示精致的分词，以及英语后缀 -ly，共同撑起这个副词；-ness 与 im- 再分别造出名词与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 污染；弄脏；玷污；亵渎；使（语言、数据等）变得不纯
definition_en: to put harmful or unwanted substances into air, water or land, or to make something impure, corrupted or ritually unclean
core_image: 一根排水管把暗色液体注进清澈的河湾，水面浮起一层油光，颜色从管口向外散开
scene: 排水管在夜里把暗色液体排进河湾，清晨水面上浮着一层油光。The factory has polluted the bay for years without a permit.
sceneCN: 这里指向水体排放有害物质、使其变脏受损（第 1 个义项：向环境排入有害物质）；句意为这家工厂多年无证污染了海湾；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「污染；污染物」
由该动词加表示「进行者、物质」的名词尾构成，义为「污染物；污染物质」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「污染者；排污者」
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「受污染的」
由该动词加现在分词词尾构成，义为「造成污染的」
由表示否定的前缀加已然形式构成，义为「未受污染的」
由表示否定的前缀加现在分词构成，义为「不造成污染的」

senses.title: To put harmful substances into the environment
senses.definition: to introduce substances or energy into air, water or soil in amounts that harm living things
senses.definitionCN: 把物质或能量引入空气、水体或土壤，其数量足以伤害生物
senses.example: Runoff from the fields has polluted the stream below the village.
senses.exampleCN: 田地的径流污染了村下游的小溪。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to soil or defile, and industry gave that soiling a physical target: air, water, ground.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本义是弄脏、玷污，工业给了这种弄脏一个物理对象：空气、水与土地。

senses.title: To make an object dirty or impure
senses.definition: to dirty or contaminate a concrete object so that it is no longer clean or usable
senses.definitionCN: 使一件具体物品变脏或混入杂质，以致不再洁净或可用
senses.example: Dust from the road polluted the open water tank.
senses.exampleCN: 路上的尘土弄脏了敞口的水箱。
senses.why: Before it named an environmental problem, the verb simply meant making a thing unclean.
senses.whyCN: 在它命名环境问题之前，这个动词只表示把东西弄得不再洁净。

senses.title: To desecrate something sacred
senses.definition: to treat a sacred place or rite as common or unclean, in religious and older legal usage
senses.definitionCN: 在宗教与旧式法律用法中，把圣地或圣礼当作凡俗或不洁之物对待
senses.example: The old law forbade anyone to pollute the spring used for the rite.
senses.exampleCN: 旧法禁止任何人玷污仪式所用的泉水。
senses.why: Defilement was a religious category long before it was a chemical one, and the verb kept that weight.
senses.whyCN: 「玷污」在成为化学范畴之前很久就是宗教范畴，这个动词保留了那份重量。

senses.title: To corrupt morals or a community
senses.definition: to degrade the moral character of a person, group or institution
senses.definitionCN: 败坏一个人、群体或制度的道德品质
senses.example: Critics claimed the broadcasts polluted the minds of the young.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者声称这些广播败坏了年轻人的心灵。
senses.why: If impurity can enter a body, it can enter a mind, and the metaphor moved from water to morals.
senses.whyCN: 既然杂质能进入身体，也能进入心灵，这个比喻就从水体移到了道德。

senses.title: To contaminate language or public debate
senses.definition: to fill speech, writing or public argument with falsehood, jargon or abuse until it loses clarity
senses.definitionCN: 让言语、文字或公共论辩充满虚假、行话或谩骂，以致失去清晰
senses.example: Readers said the comment threads had polluted the debate beyond repair.
senses.exampleCN: 读者说这些评论区已经把讨论污染到无法修复。
senses.why: Language is treated as a shared medium like water, and bad content spreads through it the same way.
senses.whyCN: 语言被当作像水一样的共享介质，坏内容以同样的方式在其中扩散。

senses.title: To disturb surroundings with noise or light
senses.titleCN: 以噪声或光干扰周围环境
senses.definition: to degrade an environment with excessive noise, artificial light or heat rather than a substance
senses.definitionCN: 用过量噪声、人工光或废热而不是物质，使环境质量下降
senses.example: The all-night floodlights polluted the darkness the moths depended on.
senses.exampleCN: 彻夜不熄的泛光灯破坏了蛾类赖以生存的黑暗环境。
senses.why: Once pollution meant any harmful addition, energy could pollute as well as matter.
senses.whyCN: 一旦污染被理解为任何有害添加，能量也能像物质一样造成污染。

senses.title: To insert errors into data or records
senses.titleCN: 在数据与记录中掺入错误
senses.definition: to add faulty, duplicated or misleading entries to a dataset or record
senses.definitionCN: 向数据集或记录中加入有误、重复或误导性的条目
senses.example: A bad script polluted the archive with thousands of duplicate rows.
senses.exampleCN: 一段有问题的脚本用成千上万条重复记录污染了档案库。
senses.why: Data is a reservoir that users share, and one bad input spreads through it.
senses.whyCN: 数据是用户共享的水库，一处坏输入就会在其中扩散。

senses.title: To contaminate water or food with pathogens
senses.titleCN: 以病原体污染水体或食物
senses.definition: to introduce bacteria, viruses or parasites into water or food so that it becomes unsafe
senses.definitionCN: 把细菌、病毒或寄生虫引入水或食物，使其不再安全
senses.example: The broken pipe polluted the well water with bacteria.
senses.exampleCN: 破裂的管道用细菌污染了井水。
senses.why: Sanitation workers used the word for germs before environmental agencies used it for chemicals.
senses.whyCN: 卫生工作者比环境机构更早用这个词来说病菌。

senses.title: To be the source of pollution
senses.titleCN: 作为污染的来源与责任方
senses.definition: to cause pollution through discharge, leakage or careless practice, said of an operator
senses.definitionCN: 因排放、泄漏或操作不慎而造成污染，用于指作业者
senses.example: The plant polluted the river while its permit was under appeal.
senses.exampleCN: 这家厂在许可证被申诉期间一直在污染这条河。
senses.why: Attribution matters legally, so the verb came to name the responsible actor as well as the act.
senses.whyCN: 归责在法律上很重要，于是这个动词也用来指负有责任的行为者，而不只是行为。

intro.en: The word came into English through French from a Latin verb meaning to defile. Its parts are a prefix meaning forth and a stem usually connected with washing, a connection that scholars state as the usual view rather than a certainty.
intro.cn: 这个词经法语从拉丁语进入英语，原义为玷污。其构成是一个表示「向前」的前缀与一个通常与「洗」相联系的词干，学界对此只说「一般认为」，并非确证。

items.en: Luere meant to wash or cleanse, and it is usually taken as the second element of the Latin verb, though the link is stated as the usual view.
items.cn: 这个词意为洗、洗净，通常被认为是该拉丁动词的第二成分，不过这一联系只按通行的看法陈述。

items.en: The prefix, an assimilated form of the prefix for forth, added the idea of movement over a surface.
items.cn: 这个前缀是表示「向前」的前缀的同化形式，加上了在表面上移动的意思。

items.en: The verb meant to defile, contaminate or dishonour, and it was used of water, places and sacred things.
items.cn: 这个动词意为玷污、污染、使蒙羞，用于水体、场所与神圣之物。

items.en: The noun named the state of defilement, and it is the direct source of the English noun.
items.cn: 这个名词指被玷污的状态，是英语名词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French carried the verb onward, and English took it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语把该动词继续传下，英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: The industrial age turned a word about defilement into a word about smoke, sewage and chemicals.
items.cn: 工业时代把关于玷污的词变成了关于烟尘、污水与化学品的词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin stem; the second group names the acts and results of contaminating.
note.cn: 第一组共用拉丁词干；第二组是表示「污染行为与结果」的相邻说法。

entries.definition: The presence of harmful substances, and the act of introducing them.
entries.definitionCN: 指有害物质的存在，也指引入这些物质的行为。

entries.definition: A substance that pollutes when it enters the environment.
entries.definitionCN: 指进入环境后造成污染的物质。

entries.definition: The person or firm responsible for the pollution.
entries.definitionCN: 指对污染负有责任的人或企业。

entries.definition: Already contaminated, used of water, soil or air.
entries.definitionCN: 指已被污染的，用于水、土壤或空气。

entries.definition: To introduce something harmful, especially germs or a chemical, into a substance or place.
entries.definitionCN: 指向某物或某地引入有害的东西，尤指病菌或化学品。

entries.definition: To make unclean or to treat something sacred with disrespect.
entries.definitionCN: 指弄脏，或以不敬的方式对待神圣之物。

entries.definition: To spoil something by adding a trace of something bad, often used of food and reputation.
entries.definitionCN: 指因混入坏东西而使事物变坏，常用于食物与名誉。

entries.definition: To make something physically unclean, the plain everyday verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指把东西弄脏的日常普通动词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the defilement sense, its recorded family and the modern environmental target.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「玷污」这一旧义、其有记录的词族与近代的环境对象。

normal.en: The Latin verb meant to defile before it meant to pollute a river, and the older weight still shows in polluted reputation.
normal.cn: 这个拉丁动词先指玷污，后指污染河流，旧有的重量仍见于「名誉被玷污」。

normal.en: Pollution, pollutant, polluter and unpolluted all grow from one stem.
normal.cn: 污染、污染物、污染者与未受污染的，都从同一词干长出。

normal.en: Pollutant ends in a different suffix from pollute, which is why the two are often misspelled.
normal.cn: 污染物一词的词尾与动词不同，这正是两者常被拼错的原因。

normal.en: Heavily polluted is the fixed phrase used in reports about rivers and air.
normal.cn: 「受到严重污染的」是关于河流与空气的报告里的固定说法。

normal.en: The prefix means forth, so the verb pictures something carried out over a surface.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「向前」，所以这个动词的画面是把东西铺到表面上。

abstract.en: Pollution is a cost pushed sideways: the maker keeps the product and gives the residue to everyone.
abstract.cn: 污染是被推向旁边的成本：制造者留下产品，把残渣交给所有人。

abstract.en: The same verb moves from water to minds to data because all three are shared media that one input can spoil.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词从水体移到心灵再移到数据，因为三者都是共享介质，一处输入就能弄坏。

abstract.en: Defilement is a boundary crossed: something clean and set apart has been made common.
abstract.cn: 玷污是一条边界被越过：本来洁净、被分隔开的东西被弄得凡俗了。

examples.en: The old smelter polluted the soil across three villages.
examples.cn: 那座旧冶炼厂污染了三个村庄的土壤。

examples.en: Discharge from the ships polluted the harbour with oil.
examples.cn: 船只的排放用油污染了港口。

examples.en: Editors warned that rumours had polluted the public record.
examples.cn: 编辑们警告说谣言已经污染了公共记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「泼路特」——泼在路上，脏水泼进河里，就把水污染了；泼脏话，就把风气玷污了

root: 拉丁语 polluere「玷污、污染」← por-（向前，pro- 的同化形式）+ 词干 luere「洗」，后半与「洗」的联系一般认为是通行看法而非确证；名词 pollutio 为直接来源。英语十四世纪经古法语借入，先指玷污与亵渎，工业时代起指对空气、水体与土壤的污染。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses keep the old weight of defilement while moving outward: water and air, objects, sacred places, morals, language, noise and light, data, germs and the responsible actor.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项保留「玷污」的旧重量并向外移动：水体与空气、器物、圣地、道德、语言、噪声与光、数据、病菌，以及负有责任的行为者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pipe pours dark liquid into a clear bay, and the colour spreads outward from the mouth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根管子把暗色液体倒进清澈的海湾，颜色从管口向外散开。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL SPOILING: harmful inputs into air, water and soil, and dirt added to a plain object.
branches.cn: 物理弄脏：有害输入进入空气、水与土壤，以及加到普通器物上的污物。

branches.en: THE INWARD DEFILEMENT: sacred places treated as common, and morals treated as a body that impurity can enter.
branches.cn: 向内的玷污：被当作凡俗的圣地，以及被当作可让杂质进入的道德。

branches.en: THE SHARED MEDIUM: language and public debate, and datasets filled with bad entries.
branches.cn: 共享介质：语言与公共讨论，以及被坏条目填满的数据集。

branches.en: THE OTHER CARRIERS: noise and light, and germs in water or food.
branches.cn: 其他载体：噪声与光，以及水体或食物中的病菌。

branches.en: THE LEDGER OF BLAME: the operator who discharges and is named as the source.
branches.cn: 责任账目：实施排放并被指名为来源的作业者。

intro.en: A prefix for forth and a stem usually read as washing make the Latin verb; English derived a whole family from it.
intro.cn: 一个表示「向前」的前缀与一个通常读作「洗」的词干构成拉丁动词，英语由此派生了一整族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the verb, its noun and its participle; the reading of the second element as washing is the usual view, not a certainty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了动词、名词与分词；把第二成分读作「洗」是通行看法，并非确证。

items.example: The verb carries the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 整个词族都由这个动词承载。

items.example: It pictures something carried out over a surface.
items.exampleCN: 它画出把东西铺到表面上的画面。

items.example: It is the usual reading of the second element.
items.exampleCN: 这是对第二成分的通行解读。

items.example: It is the recorded direct source.
items.exampleCN: 它是有记录的直接来源。

items.example: It makes the word for a polluting substance.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示污染物质的词。

items.example: It makes the word for the responsible party.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示责任方的词。

items.example: It marks water or air that is still clean.
items.exampleCN: 它标记仍然洁净的水或空气。

由该动词加表示作用物的名词词尾构成，义为「污染物」

definition_zh: 污染；污染状态；有害物质或能量进入环境并造成损害
definition_en: the introduction of harmful substances or energy into the environment, or the state of being damaged by them
core_image: 河湾水面浮着一层彩色油光，岸边芦苇被塑料绳缠住，清水已成危险之物
scene: 河湾的水面漂着一层彩色油光，岸边芦苇被塑料绳缠住。Pollution had turned the once clear river into a hazard.
sceneCN: 这里 pollution 指「水体受到有害物质侵入而变坏的状态」（第 4 个义项：水污染使水体失去原有用途）；句意为污染把曾经清澈的河变成了危险之地。图中可辨识物件：河湾、油光水膜、塑料绳、芦苇；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 污染；污染状态（不可数为主，复数指多种或多次污染）

senses.title: Harmful matter or energy entering the environment
senses.titleCN: 有害物质或能量进入环境
senses.definition: the act of putting harmful substances or excess energy into air, water or soil
senses.definitionCN: 把有害物质或过量能量放入空气、水体或土壤的行为
senses.example: Pollution had turned the once clear river into a hazard.
senses.exampleCN: 污染把曾经清澈的河变成了危险之地。
senses.why: The word names the act before it names the result: something is put into a medium that was not there before.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先命名动作，再命名结果：某物被放进了本来没有它的介质里。

senses.title: The damaged state of a medium
senses.definition: the condition of air, water or land after harmful matter has entered it
senses.definitionCN: 空气、水或土地在有害物质进入之后所处的状态
senses.example: The lake's pollution was visible as a green scum.
senses.exampleCN: 湖水的污染表现为一层绿色浮沫。
senses.why: English uses the same noun for the act and its result, so pollution can be what was done and what is now there.
senses.whyCN: 英语用同一个名词兼指动作与结果，因此 pollution 既可以是「做了什么」，也可以是「现在有什么」。

senses.title: Air pollution
senses.definition: the presence of smoke, gases or particles in the air at harmful concentrations
senses.definitionCN: 烟、气体或颗粒以有害浓度存在于空气中
senses.example: Winter air pollution settles over the plain and hides the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 冬季的空气污染压在平原上，把群山遮住。
senses.why: Coal smoke made this sense the first and most visible kind of pollution in industrial cities.
senses.whyCN: 煤烟使这个义项成为工业城市里最早、最可见的一种污染。

senses.title: Water pollution
senses.definition: the entry of sewage, chemicals or waste into rivers, lakes, groundwater or the sea
senses.definitionCN: 污水、化学品或废物进入河流、湖泊、地下水或海洋
senses.example: Water pollution from the tannery reached the wells downstream.
senses.exampleCN: 制革厂造成的水污染波及下游的水井。
senses.why: Water carries harm away from the source, so the word stresses the medium that spreads it.
senses.whyCN: 水把危害从源头带走，这个词于是强调传播它的介质。

senses.title: Soil and land pollution
senses.definition: the accumulation of harmful substances in soil, or the degradation of land by waste
senses.definitionCN: 有害物质在土壤中累积，或土地因废物而退化
senses.example: Soil pollution kept the allotments out of use for years.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤污染让这些菜地多年不能使用。
senses.why: Soil holds what air and water deliver, so pollution here is a deposit that stays in place.
senses.whyCN: 土壤承接空气与水送来的东西，这里的污染是留在原地的沉积。

senses.title: Noise, light and heat pollution
senses.definition: excess energy that harms health, wildlife or the quality of a place without adding substance
senses.definitionCN: 过量的能量，不添加物质却危害健康、野生生物或环境品质
senses.example: Light pollution erased the stars above the coastal towns.
senses.exampleCN: 光污染抹去了沿海城镇上空的星空。
senses.why: Modern regulation widened the word to energy, because harm does not require a material to be present.
senses.whyCN: 现代监管把这个词扩展到能量，因为造成危害并不需要有物质在场。

senses.title: Plastic and marine pollution
senses.definition: the accumulation of persistent waste, especially plastics, in oceans and on shores
senses.definitionCN: 持久性废物、尤其是塑料，在海洋与海岸上的累积
senses.example: Marine pollution washed ashore as bottle caps and netting.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋污染以瓶盖和网绳的形式冲上岸。
senses.why: A single material became so dominant that it earned its own use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 单一材料变得如此突出，以至于单独占用了这个词的一种用法。

senses.title: Ritual or moral defilement
senses.definition: the historical sense of making something sacred or pure unclean
senses.definitionCN: 使神圣或纯洁之物变得不洁的旧义
senses.example: The old texts speak of pollution that required a rite of cleansing.
senses.exampleCN: 古籍中说到需要行洁净礼才能解除的玷污。
senses.why: The word entered English as a religious term, and the environmental sense is a later branch of the same image.
senses.whyCN: 这个词以宗教术语进入英语，环境义是同一意象后来分出的枝。

senses.title: Abstract: degradation of information or discourse
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：信息与言论环境的变质
senses.definition: a transferred use for the flooding of a field with false, low-quality or manipulative content
senses.definitionCN: 转指某领域被虚假、低质或操纵性内容淹没
senses.example: Information pollution makes a reliable source harder to find.
senses.exampleCN: 信息污染使可靠来源更难找到。
senses.why: The metaphor preserves the structure: a shared medium is filled with something that lowers its value for everyone.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了结构：共用的介质被填入某物，使它对所有人都贬值。

intro.en: Pollution came to English through French from Latin pollutio, a noun of defilement. Its oldest English sense is religious; the environmental sense is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pollution 经法语来自拉丁 pollutio，是一个表示「玷污」的名词。它最早的英语义项是宗教性的，环境义则是近代的。年代均为约数。

items.en: The verb behind the noun is usually divided into por- (a form of pro- 'forth') and luere 'to wash'. The deeper origin of luere is uncertain, and the relation sometimes drawn to lavare 'to wash' is a related-form hypothesis, not a proved descent.
items.cn: 这个名词背后的动词通常拆成 por-（pro-「向前」的一种形式）与 luere「洗」。luere 的更深来源不确定，有人把它与 lavare「洗」联系，那只是「相关形式」的假说，并非已证实的承继。

items.en: Polluere meant 'to defile, to corrupt'. How the washing element came to mean defiling is not fully explained; one account treats the prefix as intensive rather than directional.
items.cn: polluere 意为「弄脏、败坏」。「洗」的成分如何转为「弄脏」，并未得到完整解释；一种说法把前缀视为加强成分而非方向成分。

items.en: Late Latin pollutio named a defiling, especially ritual uncleanness, and this is the sense that entered English.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 pollutio 指玷污，尤指仪式上的不洁，进入英语的正是这一义项。

items.en: From the fourteenth century English pollution meant the desecration of sacred things or the state of being ritually unclean.
items.cn: 从十四世纪起，英语 pollution 指对神圣之物的亵渎或仪式上的不洁状态。

items.en: In the nineteenth century smoke, sewage and factory waste gave the word its modern environmental sense, and it soon became a public-health issue.
items.cn: 十九世纪，烟、污水与工厂废料赋予这个词现代环境义，它很快成为公共卫生议题。

items.en: Source uncertain (internal history of polluere, first date of the environmental sense): the semantic path from washing to defiling is unexplained and the first environmental citation is not fixed, so its date is approximate; any older form offered for luere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（polluere 的内部构造、环境义的首见年代）：从「洗」到「弄脏」的语义路径未获解释，环境义的最早书证也无定论，年代只能约计；凡为 luere 给出的更早形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same pollute stock that differ in grammar or role; group two holds other words for environmental damage, each naming a different part of the problem.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 pollute 词干、语法角色不同的形式；第二组是其他表示环境损害的词，各自命名问题的一个不同部分。

entries.definition: A single offending substance; pollution is the resulting condition or the whole accumulation.
entries.definitionCN: 一种肇事的物质；pollution 是造成的结果或整体累积。

entries.definition: To put harmful matter into a medium; the noun names what the verb produces.
entries.definitionCN: 把有害物质放入介质；名词指动词所产生的状态。

entries.definition: A person or firm that pollutes; it is a responsible party, not a condition.
entries.definitionCN: 造成污染的人或企业；它是责任方，而非状态。

entries.definition: A head, a vote survey or a hornless beast, from Middle English polle; the resemblance to pollute is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 指头、投票调查或无角牲畜，出自中古英语 polle；与 pollute 的相似只是偶然。

entries.definition: The making impure of a substance or product; it need not harm an ecosystem, which pollution implies.
entries.definitionCN: 使物质或产品不纯；它未必危害生态，而 pollution 含有这一层。

entries.definition: A general lowering of quality or condition; pollution is one cause of environmental degradation.
entries.definitionCN: 品质或状况的普遍下降；污染是环境退化的一个原因。

entries.definition: The release of a substance into the air; pollution is the harm that follows from such releases.
entries.definitionCN: 物质向空气的排放；pollution 是这类排放带来的危害。

entries.definition: The clogging or dirtying of equipment, hulls or beds; it is a practical nuisance sense, not a public-health one.
entries.definitionCN: 设备、船体或床层的堵塞与污损；它是设备层面的麻烦义，而非公共卫生义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Pollution is the noun of pollute: the act of putting harm into a medium and the state that follows.
normal.cn: pollution 是 pollute 的名词：把危害放入介质的动作，以及随之而来的状态。

normal.en: The family runs pollute, pollutant, polluter, polluted and polluting.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 pollute、pollutant、polluter、polluted 与 polluting。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the medium: air pollution, water pollution, soil pollution, noise pollution.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出介质：空气污染、水污染、土壤污染、噪声污染。

normal.en: The oldest English sense was religious: pollution meant ritual uncleanness before it meant smoke.
normal.cn: 最早的英语义项是宗教性的：pollution 先指仪式上的不洁，后指烟尘。

normal.en: Poll looks alike but means 'head', so it is a false relative.
normal.cn: poll 形似而同源无关，意为「头」，是假同源。

abstract.en: Picture a clear river receiving one pipe and losing its colour downstream.
abstract.cn: 想象一条清河接入一根管子，下游就失了颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a night sky erased by a ring of lamps.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈路灯抹掉了夜空。

abstract.en: Picture a library shelf filled with books that repeat nonsense.
abstract.cn: 想象书架上塞满反复讲胡话的书。

examples.en: Pollution in the estuary comes from farms far upstream.
examples.cn: 河口处的污染来自远在上游的农田。

examples.en: The city monitors pollution every hour at ten stations.
examples.cn: 该市在十个监测站每小时监测污染。

examples.en: Noise pollution from the highway reaches the school.
examples.cn: 公路的噪声污染传到了学校。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pollute（污染）+ ion」——把脏东西放进环境这件事，以及它造成的状态 → 污染

root: 拉丁 pollutio「玷污」< polluere「弄脏」；polluere 通常拆为 por-（pro- 变体）+ luere「洗」，但「洗」转为「弄脏」未获完整解释，luere 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one intrusion: a clean medium is entered, its state changes, each medium gets its own name, energy and waste join the list, and the old religious image survives at one end while the metaphor of a spoiled shared medium survives at the other.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一次侵入展开：洁净介质被进入，状态改变，各介质各得一名，能量与废物加入清单，一端留着旧的宗教意象，另一端留着「共用介质被弄坏」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an oily sheen on a river bend, with reeds tangled in plastic cord.
core.cn: 核心意象：河湾上一层油光，芦苇缠着塑料绳。

branches.en: ACT AND STATE: English uses one noun for the putting-in and for what is left afterwards.
branches.cn: 动作与状态：英语用同一个名词兼指「放入」与「放入后剩下的」。

branches.en: THREE MEDIA: air, water and soil each make pollution visible in a different way.
branches.cn: 三种介质：空气、水与土壤各以不同方式让污染显形。

branches.en: ADDED ENERGY AND WASTE: noise, light and plastic all fit the same frame of something extra.
branches.cn: 能量与废物：噪声、光与塑料都落在「多出来的东西」这同一框架里。

branches.en: OLD ROOT: ritual defilement is the image from which the environmental sense grew.
branches.cn: 旧根：仪式上的玷污是环境义从中长出的意象。

branches.en: NEW ROOT: information pollution repeats the image in a shared medium of thought.
branches.cn: 新枝：信息污染在同一意象上重复，只是介质成了共用的思想空间。

intro.en: Pollution is a Latin noun of action with a debated root, so the suffix and prefix are clear while the semantic history of the root is not.
intro.cn: pollution 是拉丁动作名词，词根有争议，因此前缀与后缀清楚，而词根的语义历史不清楚。

latinIntro.en: Latin polluere gives pollute, pollution, pollutant and polluter; -io, -ionis forms nouns of action in English -ion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 polluere 衍生 pollute、pollution、pollutant 与 polluter；-io, -ionis 在英语中构成 -ion 动作名词。

items.example: One account reads the prefix as directional.
items.exampleCN: 一种说法把这个前缀读作方向性的。

items.example: The washing element is the disputed half of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 「洗」这个成分是动词中有争议的一半。

items.example: Polluere named both ritual and physical uncleanness.
items.exampleCN: polluere 兼指仪式与物理上的不洁。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a noun of action.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成动作名词。

items.meaning: a defiling; the state of being defiled

items.exampleCN: 受污染的小溪流着黑水。
造成污染的燃料被征税。

definition_zh: 池塘；鱼塘；养殖池；冷却池；大西洋（口语）
definition_en: a small area of still water, often made by people; also a managed basin for fish or for industrial water, and informally the Atlantic Ocean
core_image: 一圈土堤围住的一小片静水，水面映着低垂的柳枝
scene: 夏末的午后，村口的柳树把影子投在水面上，几只鸭子慢慢划过。Behind the mill, willow branches hung low over a quiet pond.
sceneCN: 这里的 pond 是「池塘」（第 1 个义项：小片静水）；句意为磨坊后面，柳枝低低地垂在一片安静的池塘上。图中可辨识物件：柳枝、水面、鸭子。

pos.zh: 池塘；鱼塘；养殖池；冷却池；大西洋（口语）

derivatives.zh: 由 pond 与 weed 复合而成，义为「池草；眼子菜类水草」
由 pond 与 side 复合而成，义为「池边的」
由 fish 与 pond 复合而成，义为「鱼塘」

senses.title: A small area of still water
senses.definition: a small area of still water, usually smaller than a lake and often dug or dammed by people
senses.definitionCN: 一片不大的静水，通常比湖小，多为人工挖成或筑堤蓄成
senses.example: Ducks floated quietly on the village pond.
senses.exampleCN: 鸭子静静地浮在村子的池塘上。
senses.why: The word began as a name for an enclosed place, and when the fence became an earth bank the same name settled on the water held inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指被围起来的地方；当围栏变成土堤，同一个名字就落到了被围在里面的水上。

senses.title: A basin kept for fish or waterfowl
senses.definition: a pond built or managed so that fish, ducks or other water animals can be raised in it
senses.definitionCN: 为养鱼、养鸭或其他水生动物而修建、管理的水体
senses.example: They dug three ponds behind the house for carp.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在屋后挖了三口鱼塘养鲤鱼。
senses.why: Once water could be held in one place, it could also be stocked, so the word widened from a patch of water to a working basin with a harvest.
senses.whyCN: 水一旦能被蓄在一处，就能往里放养生物，于是词义从一片水面扩展到有收成的生产水体。

senses.title: An engineered basin for a process
senses.definition: a basin built to hold water for cooling, settling or storing waste in an industrial process
senses.definitionCN: 工业生产中用来冷却、沉淀或存放废水的池子
senses.example: The plant pumps warm water into a cooling pond.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂把温水抽进冷却池。
senses.why: Industry borrowed the word for any shallow basin that holds liquid, keeping the old shape of water shut in by a rim.
senses.whyCN: 工业借用了这个词来指任何盛液体的浅池，保留的仍是「水被边沿围住」这一古老形状。

senses.title: The Atlantic, in casual speech
senses.definition: the Atlantic Ocean, used informally by people on one side of it when speaking of the other side
senses.definitionCN: 大西洋的口语说法，岸这边的人用它来指对岸
senses.example: She moved across the pond twenty years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 她二十年前搬到了大西洋对岸。
senses.why: Calling an ocean a pond is a deliberate understatement: two shores are treated as the banks of one small sheet of water, which makes the distance sound crossable.
senses.whyCN: 把大洋叫作池塘是故意的轻描淡写：两岸被当成一小片水的两个边，遥远的距离听起来就像能一步跨过。

intro.en: Pond first named a fenced place, then the water held behind a bank, and only later any small still water.
intro.cn: pond 最早指围起来的地方，随后指土堤拦住的水，最后才泛指任何小片静水。

items.en: The element pund- appears in pundfald, a pen for stray cattle, and meant an enclosed place rather than water.
items.cn: 古英语中的 pund- 见于 pundfald（关牲口的围栏），指的是被围起来的地方，与水无关。

items.en: Middle English ponde named an artificial body of water, typically a small lake held back by an earth bank.
items.cn: 中古英语的 ponde 指人工蓄起的水体，通常是被土堤拦住的小湖。

items.en: The enclosing fence of the old word was replaced by the bank of the pond, so the boundary stayed and the contents changed from animals to water.
items.cn: 旧词里围住场地的栅栏被池塘的土堤取代，边界还在，围住的东西却从牲口变成了水。

items.en: Modern English pond covers any small still water, whether dug for gardens, stocked with fish or built for a factory.
items.cn: 现代英语的 pond 泛指任何小片静水，无论是为花园挖的、养鱼的，还是给工厂建的。

items.en: The teasing phrase across the pond turns the Atlantic into a small sheet of water, and compounds such as cooling pond extend the word to industry.
items.cn: 玩笑说法 across the pond 把大西洋说成一小片水；cooling pond 这类复合词则把词义延伸到工业。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short English words that differ from pond by a single letter; the near-meaning group gathers other names for still water.
note.cn: 形近组收与 pond 只差一两个字母的短词；近义组收其他表示静水的词。

entries.definition: A unit of weight or money, or an enclosure for animals; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 重量或货币单位，也指关动物的围栏；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Feeling affection or liking for someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 喜爱某人的；钟情的。

entries.definition: Something that ties people together, or a certificate of debt.
entries.definitionCN: 纽带；债券。

entries.definition: A sum of money kept for a special purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定用途保存的一笔钱；基金。

entries.definition: A lake or a small sheet of still water, now mostly used in literary writing and place names.
entries.definitionCN: 湖或小片静水，如今多见于文学描写与地名。

entries.definition: A small shallow patch of rainwater on the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 地面上由雨水积成的小浅水洼。

entries.definition: A large area of water surrounded by land.
entries.definitionCN: 被陆地环绕的大片水域；湖。

entries.definition: A large artificial lake used for storing water.
entries.definitionCN: 用于蓄水的大型人工湖；水库。

normalIntro.en: Pond is a word about a boundary: an enclosed place became an enclosed sheet of water, and the compounds show what people keep inside it.
normalIntro.cn: pond 是一个关于边界的词：被围住的地方变成了被围住的水面，而各类复合词则显示人们往里面放什么。

normal.en: Old English pundfald was a pen for cattle, so the earliest sense of the family is a fenced space, not a wet one.
normal.cn: 古英语 pundfald 是关牛的围栏，所以这一族词最早的意思是围起来的空间，而不是水。

normal.en: A pond is what you get when the fence around a place is replaced by a bank around water.
normal.cn: 当围住场地的栅栏换成围住水的土堤，得到的就是 pond。

normal.en: Fishpond and duck pond simply name the animals kept inside, which is the cheapest way to remember the word.
normal.cn: fishpond 与 duck pond 直接把养在里面的动物写出来，这是记住这个词最省力的办法。

normal.en: Pondweed grows where ponds are, so the compound -weed tells you the plant's home rather than its shape.
normal.cn: pondweed 长在池塘里，所以 -weed 这个复合成分告诉你的是植物的住处，而不是它的形状。

normal.en: Across the pond works because two coasts can be imagined as the two banks of one small stretch of water.
normal.cn: across the pond 之所以成立，是因为两岸可以被想象成一小片水的两个岸。

abstract.en: Every pond is a decision to stop water from moving on, which is why the word sits so close to dams and banks.
abstract.cn: 每个池塘都是「不让水继续流走」的决定，所以这个词总跟堤坝、岸沿挨在一起。

abstract.en: A word that once meant a fence now means a surface, a sign that boundaries outlive the things they were built for.
abstract.cn: 一个曾指栅栏的词如今指一片水面，说明边界往往比它当初围的东西活得更久。

abstract.en: Shrinking an ocean to a pond is language doing what maps cannot: making distance feel small enough to joke about.
abstract.cn: 把大洋缩成池塘，是语言做了地图做不到的事：让距离小到可以拿来开玩笑。

examples.en: The farm keeps a pond for ducks and carp.
examples.cn: 这个农场留了一口池塘养鸭子和鲤鱼。

examples.en: Willow branches brushed the surface of the pond.
examples.cn: 柳枝拂过池塘的水面。

examples.en: Her sister has lived across the pond for years.
examples.cn: 她姐姐在大西洋对岸住了很多年。

senses.title: A small body of still water
senses.definition: a small area of still water, either left by rain or made by people
senses.definitionCN: 一小片不流动的水，或由雨水积成，或由人工砌成
senses.example: Rainwater collected in a shallow pool beside the road.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水在路边积成了一个浅浅的水洼。
senses.why: Old English pol named still water and the deep spots in a river, so the word starts from water that stays put instead of running on.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 pol 指静水以及河中的深水处，所以这个词的起点是不往前流、留在原地的水。

senses.title: A basin built for swimming
senses.definition: an artificial basin filled with water and used for swimming
senses.definitionCN: 灌满水、供人游泳的人工水池
senses.example: The children swam in the hotel pool all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们整个下午都在旅馆的泳池里游泳。
senses.why: A pool is water held in one place, so a basin built to hold it for swimming needs no new word, only a purpose added in front.
senses.whyCN: pool 本来就是蓄在一处的水，因此供游泳的水池不必另造新词，只需在前面加一个用途。

senses.title: A shared supply of money or people
senses.definition: an amount of money, work or people contributed by many and used by all of them
senses.definitionCN: 由多方拿出、供大家共同使用的钱、工作或人力
senses.example: The company draws from a large pool of engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司从庞大的人才库中选用工程师。
senses.why: The game sense came from French poule, a common stake, and that shared pot of money gave English the idea of any supply that many people pay into and draw from.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项来自法语 poule（大家押下的赌注），那口公用的钱罐让英语引申出「众人凑入、众人取用」的资源。

senses.title: To gather things into one shared whole
senses.definition: to put money, effort or equipment together so that a group can use it
senses.definitionCN: 把钱、力气或设备合在一起，供一群人共同使用
senses.example: The two firms pooled their resources to finish the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司集中资源，才把这座桥修完。
senses.why: If a pool is a common pot, the verb is simply the act of filling it: each side drops something in before anyone draws anything out.
senses.whyCN: 如果 pool 是一口公用的罐子，动词就是往罐里放东西的动作：各方先各放一点，之后才谈取用。

senses.title: A table game played with cues
senses.definition: a game played on a cloth-covered table in which balls are struck with a long cue
senses.definitionCN: 在铺布球台上用长杆击球的游戏
senses.example: They spent the evening playing pool.
senses.exampleCN: 他们打了一晚上台球。
senses.why: In French poule the stakes were pooled before play, and the table game kept the name of that shared bet rather than any word for water.
senses.whyCN: 法语 poule 指开局前把赌注合在一起，这种球戏留下的是「公共赌注」的名字，与水毫无关系。

intro.en: Pool has two streams: an Old English word for still water, and a French word for a common stake that gave English the shared-fund and billiard senses.
intro.cn: pool 有两条来路：一条是古英语中表示静水的词，另一条是法语中表示公共赌注的词，后者带来「共用资金」与「台球」两个义项。

items.en: Old English pol meant a small body of water and could also name a deep, slow spot in a river.
items.cn: 古英语的 pol 指一小片水，也可指河中水深流缓的地方。

items.en: Related forms appear in Middle Dutch poel and Old High German pfuol, but the earlier origin of the set is uncertain.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 poel 与古高地德语 pfuol 有相关形式，但这组词更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Middle English pool broadened to ponds, mill dams and any still water, natural or dug.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pool 扩展到池塘、磨坊水坝以及任何静水，无论天然还是人工。

items.en: French poule, literally a hen, named the stakes that card players put into one pot, and English borrowed the word for that common fund.
items.cn: 法语 poule 本义是母鸡，用来指牌戏玩家押进同一口罐子的赌注，英语借来表示这笔公共的钱。

items.en: From card tables the shared-fund sense spread to typing pools and car pools, while the cue game kept the name of the pooled stakes.
items.cn: 从牌桌出发，「公共资金」义扩展到打字员组、拼车等说法，而用球杆玩的游戏则留下了「公共赌注」这个名字。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers one-syllable words that differ from pool by a letter; the near-meaning group gathers other containers and bodies of water.
note.cn: 形近组收与 pool 只差一个字母的单音节词；近义组收其他盛水之处与水体。

normalIntro.en: Pool joins two old ideas, still water and a common stake, and almost every sense can be reached from one of them.
normalIntro.cn: pool 把两个古老的意思合在一起：静水与公共赌注；几乎每个义项都能从其中之一走到。

normal.en: Old English pol meant still water and a deep spot in a river, which is why the water senses need no explanation.
normal.cn: 古英语 pol 指静水与河中的深水处，所以与水有关的义项不需要额外解释。

normal.en: French poule literally means hen; it named the stakes players pushed into one pot, and that pot became the shared fund.
normal.cn: 法语 poule 本义是母鸡，指玩家押进同一口罐子的赌注，这口罐子后来成了共用资金。

normal.en: A talent pool and a gene pool both use the image of a common supply that people or traits are drawn from.
normal.cn: talent pool 与 gene pool 用的都是「公共储备」这个意象，人或性状从中取用。

normal.en: Pool resources is the verb built from the pot: put in first, take out later, and the group gains what no one had alone.
normal.cn: pool resources 是从那口罐子来的动词：先放进去，后面再取，群体便得到了单个人没有的东西。

normal.en: Pool table keeps the gambling name, not the water name, which is why billiards has nothing to do with swimming.
normal.cn: pool table 保留的是赌博的名字，不是水的名字，所以台球与游泳无关。

abstract.en: Water that stops moving and money that stops circulating in private hands follow the same shape: something gathered into one place.
abstract.cn: 停止流动的水，与不再留在私人手里的钱，形状相同：都是被聚到一处的东西。

abstract.en: A pool is a promise that what is put in will be shared out, whether it holds water, money or engineers.
abstract.cn: pool 是一种承诺：放进去的东西会被分用，无论里面装的是水、钱还是工程师。

abstract.en: Two unrelated histories meeting in one spelling is a reminder that a word can carry more than one memory.
abstract.cn: 两段毫不相干的历史挤进同一个拼写，提醒人一个词可以同时带着不止一段记忆。

sceneCN: 这里的 poor 是「贫穷的」（第 1 个义项：缺钱）；句意为那个冬天这家人穷得买不起煤。图中可辨识物件：短了一截的外套、磨白的袖口、没有暖气的屋子。
