senses.title: Having very little money
senses.definition: having so little money that ordinary needs such as food, heat or clothing are hard to meet
senses.definitionCN: 钱少到难以应付吃饭、取暖、穿衣这类日常需要
senses.example: The family was too poor to heat the house.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人穷得连房子都供不起暖气。
senses.why: Latin pauper described a person of small means, and the word came into English through French carrying that plain material sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pauper 形容家底微薄的人，这个词经法语进入英语时，带的就是这层朴素的物质含义。

senses.title: Of low quality
senses.definition: not as good as it should be in strength, sound, finish or standard
senses.definitionCN: 在结实、清晰、做工或水准上达不到应有的程度
senses.example: The recording was poor and hard to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 录音效果很差，听不太清楚。
senses.why: A person can be poor in money, so a thing can be poor in what it ought to have; the same measure of lack is applied to quality.
senses.whyCN: 人可以穷在钱上，东西也可以穷在它本该有的地方；判断质量用的仍是同一把「缺」的尺子。

senses.title: Deserving pity
senses.definition: unfortunate enough to make other people feel sorry for them
senses.definitionCN: 处境不幸，使别人替其难过
senses.example: The poor dog waited in the rain for its owner.
senses.exampleCN: 那只可怜的狗在雨里等着主人。
senses.why: Someone who has too little is exposed to harm, so the word slides from naming the lack to naming the feeling that lack stirs in others.
senses.whyCN: 拥有的太少就容易受伤害，于是这个词从指「缺」滑向指「缺」在旁人心里激起的怜惜。

senses.title: Lacking a needed substance
senses.definition: containing too little of something that plants or bodies need, as in poor soil or water poor in minerals
senses.definitionCN: 所含的植物或身体所需之物太少，如贫瘠的土壤、缺少矿物质的水
senses.example: This soil is too poor for wheat.
senses.exampleCN: 这土太贫瘠，种不了小麦。
senses.why: The oldest frame survives in phrases such as poor in iron, where the word simply marks what a thing does not have enough of.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的结构留在 poor in iron 这类说法里，那里的 poor 只是标出一件东西哪一样不够。

intro.en: Poor comes from Latin pauper through Old French, and the whole family keeps the idea of having or producing too little.
intro.cn: poor 经古法语来自拉丁语 pauper，整族词都保留着「拥有或产出太少」的意思。

items.en: Pauper meant poor or of small means, and it could even describe soil that yields little.
items.cn: pauper 意为贫穷的、家底薄的，甚至能形容产出很少的土地。

items.en: The noun paupertas named poverty and want, and it is the source of the English word poverty.
items.cn: 名词 paupertas 指贫困与匮乏，是英语 poverty 的来源。

items.en: Old French povre kept both the material sense and a stronger tone of wretchedness and misfortune.
items.cn: 古法语的 povre 既保留物质上的贫穷，也带有更重的凄惨与不幸意味。

items.en: Middle English spellings such as povre and poure competed, and the form with -ou- became the standard poor.
items.cn: 中古英语的 povre、poure 等拼写并行，带 -ou- 的形式最终成为标准拼写 poor。

items.en: Modern English extended the word from money to quality, health, soil and finally to a tone of pity.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义从钱财扩展到质量、健康、土壤，最后还带上了一层怜悯的语气。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words sharing the Latin stem or the sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for having little, being bad or deserving pity.
note.cn: 形近组收共享拉丁词干或读音相近的词；近义组收表示「贫穷」「差」「可怜」的词。

normalIntro.cn: poor 是拉丁语中表示「家底薄」的词，它这一族显示了关于钱的判断如何变成关于质量的判断，再变成怜悯。

normal.en: Pauper is the Latin word itself used as an English noun: a pauper is a person who is poor.
normal.cn: pauper 就是那个拉丁词直接当英语名词用：a pauper 就是穷人。

normal.en: Poverty comes from Latin paupertas, the noun built beside pauper, so the two words are cousins rather than parent and child.
normal.cn: poverty 来自拉丁语 paupertas，是与 pauper 并列造出的名词，所以两者是表亲，而不是父子。

normal.en: Old French povre lost its ending on the way into English, leaving the short form poor.
normal.cn: 古法语的 povre 在进入英语的路上丢掉了词尾，留下短短的 poor。

normal.en: Poor quality and poor health both keep the original idea of lacking what should be there.
normal.cn: poor quality 与 poor health 都保留了原来的意思：缺了本该有的东西。

normal.en: The poor is an adjective standing in for a noun, so it takes a plural verb: the poor are, not the poor is.
normal.cn: the poor 是形容词顶替名词，所以配复数动词：说 the poor are，不说 the poor is。

abstract.en: A word for having too little turns into a word for being bad, which shows how easily a judgement about means becomes a judgement about worth.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「拥有太少」的词变成了表示「不好」的词，说明对家底的判断多容易变成对价值的判断。

abstract.en: Calling a dog poor does not measure its money; it measures the gap between what it has and what it needs.
abstract.cn: 把一只狗叫作 poor，量的不是它的钱，而是它拥有的与它需要的之间的差距。

abstract.en: Poor soil and a poor excuse share one grammar: something is missing that the situation requires.
abstract.cn: 贫瘠的土壤与蹩脚的借口共用一个语法：这情形需要的东西缺了。

sensesIntro.en: The core is having too little; the branches apply that lack to money, to quality, to the feeling of pity, and to soil or water short of a substance.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「拥有的太少」；各分支把这种「缺」分别用到钱财、质量、怜悯之情，以及缺某种成分的土壤或水。

definition_en: popular music as a genre; a short sharp bursting sound; to burst or open with such a sound; and to appear or go somewhere suddenly
core_image: 手臂边一只气球突然炸开，碎片飞出去，屋里的人全都抬头
scene: 街角的小店门口挂着旧音箱，午后的阳光斜进来，一群学生跟着旋律点头。The radio kept playing one pop song after another while the students waited for the bus.
sceneCN: 这里 pop 指「流行音乐」（第 1 个义项：旋律好记、面向大众的音乐）；句意为学生们等公交时，收音机一首接一首地放着流行歌。图中可辨识物件：旧音箱、斜照进来的阳光、等车的学生。

pos.zh: 爆开；突然冒出；匆匆去一趟

derivatives.zh: 由 pop 与 corn 复合而成，取「受热爆开」的旧义，义为「爆米花」
由 pop 加表示工具或人的 -er 构成，义为「爆米花锅；按扣」
由 pop 加 -ing 构成，义为「连续的爆响；机械舞」

senses.title: Popular music as a genre
senses.definition: a style of music with a strong beat and easily remembered tunes, made for a wide audience rather than for specialists
senses.definitionCN: 节奏鲜明、旋律好记，面向广大听众而非专业圈子的音乐类型
senses.example: She sang along to every pop song on the radio.
senses.exampleCN: 收音机里每一首流行歌她都跟着唱。
senses.why: This sense is a mid-twentieth-century clipping of popular, taken from phrases such as popular music, so the name says who the music is made for rather than how it is composed.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是二十世纪中叶从 popular 截短来的，取的是 popular music 一类说法，所以名字说的是音乐做给谁听，而不是它怎么写。

senses.title: A short sharp bursting sound
senses.definition: a small explosive noise made when something bursts, snaps or is struck
senses.definitionCN: 东西爆开、绷断或被击中时发出的短促爆响
senses.example: The paper bag gave a loud pop when she hit it.
senses.exampleCN: 她一巴掌拍下去，纸袋砰地响了一声。
senses.why: This sense is generally taken to be imitative: the word copies the noise of a small burst, which is why one form can name both the sound and the event behind it.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项一般认为来自拟声：词本身在模仿小东西爆开的声响，所以同一种形式既能指声音，也能指发出声音的那件事。

senses.title: To burst or open with a sharp sound
senses.definition: to burst, open or come out suddenly with a small sharp noise
senses.definitionCN: 伴随着短促响声突然爆开、弹开或冒出来
senses.example: The cork popped out of the bottle and hit the ceiling.
senses.exampleCN: 瓶塞砰地从瓶口弹出来，撞到了天花板上。
senses.why: Once the sound-word had named the noise of bursting, English could turn it into a verb for whatever produced that noise, and a cork leaving a bottle is the clearest case.
senses.whyCN: 拟声词一旦指认了爆裂的响声，英语就能把它变成动词，指发出这声响的东西；瓶塞飞出瓶口就是最清楚的例子。

senses.title: To appear or go somewhere suddenly
senses.definition: to come into view suddenly and briefly, or to go somewhere quickly for a short time
senses.definitionCN: 突然而短暂地出现在眼前，或很快地去某处一趟
senses.example: A rabbit popped out of the hole and froze.
senses.exampleCN: 一只兔子突然从洞里冒出来，随即定住不动。
senses.why: A burst is sudden and over in a moment; English carries that suddenness over to anything that appears or leaves in a flash, which is how the verb reaches rabbits and short errands.
senses.whyCN: 爆开是一下子发生、一下就结束的；英语把这种突然挪到任何一闪而现或一闪而去的事情上，动词于是能用来说兔子，也能说匆匆跑一趟。

intro.en: English has two words written pop: an imitative syllable for a bang, and a twentieth-century clipping of popular. The spellings merged, the histories did not.
intro.cn: 英语里有两个拼作 pop 的词：一个模仿爆响，一个是二十世纪对 popular 的截短。拼写合流了，来历并没有合流。

items.en: Populus named the people as a body, the crowd whose taste decides what becomes common.
items.cn: populus 指作为整体的民众，也就是他们的喜好决定了什么东西会变得普遍。

items.en: Popularis meant belonging to or pleasing the people, and it is the adjective that pop would later shorten.
items.cn: popularis 意为属于民众的、讨民众喜欢的，正是后来被 pop 截短的那个形容词。

items.en: Generally regarded as imitative, the short word for a small explosion copies the sound itself and has no connection with Latin.
items.cn: 一般认为表示小爆炸的 pop 是拟声词，直接模仿声音，与拉丁语没有关系。

items.en: In the mid-twentieth century popular music was clipped to pop, used first as a modifier and soon as a noun in its own right.
items.cn: 二十世纪中叶，popular music 被截短成 pop，先作修饰语，很快又独立作名词。

items.en: Modern English keeps both strands: a bang, a quick errand and a whole shelf of music, all spelled the same way.
items.cn: 现代英语两条线都留着：一声爆响、一趟快去快回、一整排音乐，拼写完全一样。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the populus family behind the music sense; the near-meaning group collects other words for popular music and for sudden movement.
note.cn: 形近组顺着音乐义背后的 populus 词族展开；近义组收表示流行音乐与突然动作的其他词。

entries.definition: Liked by many people; the adjective that pop shortens.
entries.definitionCN: 受许多人喜爱的；pop 正是它的截短形式。

entries.definition: The state of being liked or accepted by many people.
entries.definitionCN: 受许多人喜爱或接受的状况。

entries.definition: To make something widely known or liked.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物广为人知或广受欢迎。

entries.definition: Corn that bursts open when it is heated.
entries.definitionCN: 受热后爆开的玉米；爆米花。

entries.definition: A loud form of popular music built on guitars and drums.
entries.definitionCN: 以吉他和鼓为主的吵闹流行音乐；摇滚。

entries.definition: A song or record that becomes very successful.
entries.definitionCN: 非常成功的歌曲或唱片；热门歌曲。

entries.definition: The music, taste or opinion accepted by most people.
entries.definitionCN: 被大多数人接受的音乐、品味或观点；主流。

normalIntro.en: The word carries two histories at once: a copied sound and a shortened adjective, and most of its uses can be traced to one or the other.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词同时背着两段来历：一个模仿来的声音，一个被截短的形容词；它的用法大多能归到其中一条。

normal.en: Popular music was shortened to pop, so a pop song is simply a song meant for everybody.
normal.cn: popular music 被缩成 pop，所以 pop song 就是给所有人听的歌。

normal.en: The bang is imitative: say the word sharply and you have already made the sound.
normal.cn: 爆响那个义项是拟声的：把这个词短促地念出来，声音就已经发出来了。

normal.en: Pop up keeps the idea of a burst: something appears as if it had just exploded into view.
normal.cn: pop up 保留了「突然爆开」的意思：某物像是刚炸出来一样出现在眼前。

normal.en: Pop into a shop applies the same suddenness to a short errand, in and out in a moment.
normal.cn: pop into a shop 把同一种突然用在短程跑腿上，进去又出来，只用一会儿。

normal.en: Popcorn is named for the moment the kernel bursts, so the compound preserves the oldest sense.
normal.cn: popcorn 得名于玉米粒爆开的那一刻，这个复合词保存了最古老的义项。

abstract.en: One syllable carries both a drum hit and a hit song: noise and culture share a spelling.
abstract.cn: 一个音节既装着鼓点的一击，也装着一首热门歌：声音和文化共用一种拼写。

abstract.en: A balloon, a cork, a rabbit: the same snap marks every sudden appearance.
abstract.cn: 气球、瓶塞、兔子：同一声脆响标记着每一次突然出现。

abstract.en: Pop is what a crowd makes common, so the word for the people sits silently inside it.
abstract.cn: pop 指人群使之变得普遍的东西，所以表示民众的那个词静静藏在它里面。

examples.en: The children danced to a pop song in the kitchen.
examples.cn: 孩子们在厨房里跟着一首流行歌跳舞。

examples.en: The balloon popped and the dog ran off.
examples.cn: 气球砰地爆了，狗跑开了。

examples.en: A message popped up on the screen.
examples.cn: 屏幕上突然弹出一条消息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泡泡」——泡泡一破就是砰的一声；pop 又是人人会哼的流行歌。

sensesIntro.en: Two origins feed one spelling: the sharp sound and its suddenness on one side, mass-market music on the other.
sensesIntro.cn: 两种来历汇成一个拼写：一边是爆响与随之而来的突然，另一边是面向大众的音乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balloon bursting at arm's length, its skin flying off while everyone looks up.
core.cn: 核心意象：手臂边上一只气球突然炸开，碎片飞出去，所有人都抬头看。

branches.en: one short word for a bang and for a hit tune
branches.cn: 一个短词同时指爆响和热门曲子

intro.en: The word rests on two layers: an imitative English syllable, and the Latin family of populus. In that family -ar builds the adjective popular, -ity builds the noun of state, and -ize builds the verb of making; pop itself is only a clipping of the -ar form.
intro.cn: 这个词压着两层东西：一个拟声的英语音节，以及拉丁语 populus 词族。在这个词族里，-ar 造形容词 popular，-ity 造表状态的名词，-ize 造表「使……」的动词；pop 本身只是那个 -ar 形容词的截短。

definition_zh: 受欢迎的；大众的；通俗的；民众的；普遍的
definition_en: liked or approved by many people; made for ordinary people rather than specialists; of the people as a political source; and held by most people
core_image: 小店门口排起长队，路过的人不知道卖什么，也先跟着排上
scene: 放学后的面馆门口总有人排队，队伍拐过墙角，连附近上班的人也来凑热闹。That noodle shop is popular with students because it is cheap and fast.
sceneCN: 这里 popular 指「受欢迎的」（第 1 个义项：被很多人喜欢）；句意为这家面馆便宜又上得快，很受学生欢迎。图中可辨识场景：排到墙角的长队、放学的学生、探头张望的路人。

pos.zh: 受欢迎的；大众的；通俗的；民众的；普遍的

derivatives.zh: 由 popular 加 -ity 构成，义为「受欢迎；人气」
由 popular 加 -ize 构成，义为「使普及；使通俗化」
由 popular 加 -ly 构成，义为「普遍地；由民众」
由 popular 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不受欢迎的」

senses.title: Liked by many people
senses.definition: liked, approved of or supported by a large number of people
senses.definitionCN: 被很多人喜欢、认可或支持的
senses.example: The new teacher quickly became popular with her class.
senses.exampleCN: 新来的老师很快就受到班上学生的欢迎。
senses.why: Latin popularis meant belonging to the people; a thing that belongs to everybody is one everybody is ready to accept, so approval grows out of that shared ownership.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 popularis 意为属于民众的；一样东西既然属于所有人，大家就都愿意接受它，「受欢迎」正是从这种共有关系里长出来的。

senses.title: Made for ordinary people
senses.definition: designed for ordinary people rather than for experts, and therefore easy to follow
senses.definitionCN: 面向普通人而非专家，因而容易听懂的
senses.example: He writes popular books about astronomy for readers with no training.
senses.exampleCN: 他写的天文读物面向没有受过专业训练的读者。
senses.why: If something is of the people, it is also for the people, so the word came to mark work that avoids the language of specialists.
senses.whyCN: 如果一样东西属于民众，自然也是做给民众的，于是这个词用来标记那些避开专家术语的作品。

senses.title: Of the people as a political source
senses.definition: relating to ordinary citizens, especially as the source of political authority
senses.definitionCN: 与普通公民有关的，尤指权力来自他们的
senses.example: The constitution was approved by a popular vote.
senses.exampleCN: 这部宪法经民众投票获得通过。
senses.why: The oldest political sense keeps the Latin meaning almost untouched: authority rests with populus, the people, not with a ruler above them.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的政治义几乎原封不动保留了拉丁含义：权力属于 populus（民众），而不是属于高居于他们之上的统治者。

senses.title: Held by most people
senses.definition: believed or repeated by a large part of the public, whether or not it is true
senses.definitionCN: 被大部分公众相信或传说的，不论真假
senses.example: It is a popular belief that we only use ten percent of our brains.
senses.exampleCN: 人们普遍相信我们只用了大脑的百分之十。
senses.why: Once an idea belongs to the many, it counts as popular even when it is wrong, which is why the word can sit directly beside belief and misconception.
senses.whyCN: 一个说法一旦属于很多人，即使它是错的也被称作 popular，所以这个词能直接修饰「看法」和「误解」。

intro.en: Popular came from Latin through French with the plain sense of belonging to the people; only later did English add the warmer sense of being liked.
intro.cn: popular 经法语来自拉丁语，本义只是「属于民众的」；「受喜爱」这层更暖的意思是很晚才由英语添上的。

items.en: Populus was the body of citizens, the people seen as a single crowd.
items.cn: populus 指公民的整体，是把人们看作一群人。

items.en: Popularis meant belonging to, pleasing or favouring the people, and it could describe a politician who courted them.
items.cn: popularis 意为属于民众的、讨民众喜欢的、站在民众一边的，也能形容讨好民众的政治人物。

items.en: Old French took the adjective as populaire, keeping both the neutral and the approving tones.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词写作 populaire，中性义与赞许义都保留着。

items.en: Middle English populere meant common, of the common people, and could still carry a hint of vulgar.
items.cn: 中古英语的 populere 意为普通的、平民的，仍可能带一点「粗俗」的意味。

items.en: Modern English pushed the word towards approval and, in politics, towards the people as the source of authority.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义推向「受认可」，在政治语境里则推向「权力来自民众」这一层。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the populus family and its negated form; the near-meaning group gathers words for being widely known or widely held.
note.cn: 形近组收 populus 词族及其否定形式；近义组收表示广为人知、广为接受的词。

entries.definition: The state or degree of being liked by many people.
entries.definitionCN: 受许多人喜爱的状态或程度。

entries.definition: To make something widely known, used or liked.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物广为人知、广为使用或广受欢迎。

entries.definition: Full of people; having a large population.
entries.definitionCN: 人口众多的；人烟稠密的。

entries.definition: Not liked or approved of by most people.
entries.definitionCN: 不被大多数人喜欢的；不受欢迎的。

entries.definition: Known by a great many people.
entries.definitionCN: 被很多人知道的；著名的。

entries.definition: Found, done or believed by most people.
entries.definitionCN: 大多数人都有的、做的或相信的；常见的。

entries.definition: Existing or happening over a large area or among many people.
entries.definitionCN: 在很大范围或许多人中存在的；普遍的。

normalIntro.en: The word begins with a Latin noun for the people, and each modern sense measures some way in which a thing belongs to them.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词起于拉丁语里表示民众的名词，每个现代义项都在衡量某样东西以何种方式属于他们。

normal.en: Latin popularis meant of the people, and being liked is simply being accepted by the people who own it.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 popularis 意为属于民众的，而「被喜欢」不过是被拥有它的那群人接受。

normal.en: Popular and population share populus: one counts approval, the other counts heads.
normal.cn: popular 与 population 共用 populus：一个数的是认可，一个数的是人头。

normal.en: Popularity is popular plus -ity, the state of being liked seen as a quantity.
normal.cn: popularity 是 popular 加 -ity，把「被喜欢」看成一种可计量的状态。

normal.en: Popularize is popular plus -ize, to make something common among people.
normal.cn: popularize 是 popular 加 -ize，让某样东西在人们中间变得普遍。

normal.en: Popular with names the crowd that likes it; popular for names the reason.
normal.cn: popular with 后面接喜欢它的人群；popular for 后面接喜欢它的原因。

abstract.en: A queue outside a small shop is popularity made visible.
abstract.cn: 小店门口的一条长队，就是看得见的人气。

abstract.en: What belongs to everyone ends up pleasing everyone, so ownership turns into affection.
abstract.cn: 属于所有人的东西，最后会让所有人喜欢，所有权就这样变成了好感。

abstract.en: A word can be popular and still be wrong, which is why belief takes the same adjective as music.
abstract.cn: 一个说法可以很流行又完全是错的，所以「看法」和音乐共用同一个形容词。

examples.en: This song is popular with children.
examples.cn: 这首歌很受孩子们欢迎。

examples.en: Popular science books explain hard ideas in plain words.
examples.cn: 科普读物用平实的语言解释难懂的概念。

examples.en: The mayor was elected by popular vote.
examples.cn: 市长是通过民众投票选出的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泡普乐」——把知识泡进普通人的快乐里，大家就都喜欢；popular 就是受欢迎的、大众的。

root: 拉丁语 populus（民众）→ popularis（属于民众的）→ 古法语 populaire → 英语 popular；同族还有 population、populace。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is belonging to the people; it then splits into being liked, being made for them, coming from them politically, and being believed by them.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「属于民众」；由此分出被他们喜欢、为他们而做、政治上来自他们，以及被他们相信。

core.cn: 核心意象：小店门口的长队拐过墙角，陌生人没问缘由也排了进去。

intro.en: A Latin noun for the people and its adjective carry the word, and the English suffixes divide the labour: -ar makes the adjective, -ity the noun of state, -ize the verb of making.
intro.cn: 一个表示民众的拉丁名词及其形容词撑起这个词，英语后缀则各管一段：-ar 造形容词，-ity 造表状态的名词，-ize 造表「使……」的动词。

definition_zh: 人口；全体居民；种群；（统计）总体
definition_en: the people living in a place, or any group of individuals counted together, including a breeding group of animals or a complete set of data
core_image: 一张城市鸟瞰图，屋顶密密麻麻，每个小点代表一个人，远处还有一片标着虫鸟的林子

senses.title: People counted together
senses.definition: the total number of people who live in a particular area, town or country
senses.definitionCN: 居住在某一地区、城镇或国家的总人数
senses.example: The population of the region passed five million last year.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的人口去年突破五百万。
senses.why: populus in Latin meant 'the people'. The suffix -ation turns the body of people into a countable quantity, so the word names people as a number.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 populus 意为“人民”。后缀 -ation 把一群人变成可计数的量，因此这个词把“人”命名为一个数字。

senses.title: The people themselves
senses.titleCN: 全体居民：住在那里的人
senses.definition: all the inhabitants of a place, thought of as a social body rather than as a statistic
senses.definitionCN: 某地的全部居民，被视为一个社会群体而非一个统计数字
senses.example: The new bus route mainly serves the rural population.
senses.exampleCN: 这条新公交线路主要服务农村居民。
senses.why: English often uses population for the living community, not merely its size. The same word shifts from number to people by context alone.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用 population 指活生生的社区，而不只是它的规模。同一个词凭语境从“数字”滑向“人群”。

senses.title: A named subgroup
senses.titleCN: 特定人群：某类人构成的那一群
senses.definition: a particular group within a larger community, such as students, patients or workers
senses.definitionCN: 较大社区中的某一特定群体，如学生、病人或劳动者
senses.example: The clinic serves a mainly elderly population.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所主要服务老年人群。
senses.why: Any bounded group can be called a population because the word only requires a set of individuals and a shared boundary.
senses.whyCN: 任何有边界的群体都可称作 population，因为这个词只要求“一群个体”加“一条共同边界”。

senses.title: Biology: one breeding group
senses.definition: in biology, a group of organisms of the same species living in one area and able to interbreed
senses.definitionCN: 生物学上指同一物种、生活在同一区域且能相互交配繁殖的一群生物
senses.example: The island population of finches has been isolated for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 岛上的雀鸟种群已隔离了几个世纪。
senses.why: Biologists borrowed the demographic word and replaced 'citizens' with 'individuals of one species'. The boundary, not the species, defines the group.
senses.whyCN: 生物学家借用了人口学的词，把“公民”换成“同一物种的个体”。界定群体的是边界，而不是物种。

senses.title: Statistics: the whole set
senses.titleCN: 统计学：总体（与样本相对）
senses.definition: in statistics, the complete set of items from which a sample is drawn
senses.definitionCN: 统计学上指被抽样的完整集合，与“样本”相对
senses.example: The sample was chosen randomly from a population of ten thousand firms.
senses.exampleCN: 样本是从一万家企业的总体中随机抽出的。
senses.why: Statistics keeps the demographic sense of 'everyone', then applies it to any complete set: once you can count a group, the group is a population.
senses.whyCN: 统计学保留“全部人”的人口学含义，再套到任何完整集合上：只要能计数一群，这群就是总体。

senses.title: Animal or plant numbers
senses.titleCN: 动植物数量：一个地区的个体量
senses.definition: the number of animals or plants of a kind in a given area, often studied as density or trend
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区某类动植物的个体数量，常以密度或变化趋势来研究
senses.example: The wolf population fell sharply after the hard winter.
senses.exampleCN: 严冬之后狼的数量大幅下降。
senses.why: The counting frame is the key: pick a place and a kind, and the word reports how many are inside it.
senses.whyCN: 关键在于计数框：选定一个地方和一个种类，这个词就报告框里有多少个。

senses.title: The act of settling
senses.titleCN: 迁入定居：使地方有人住（旧义）
senses.definition: the act of filling an area with inhabitants, now mostly expressed by the related verb
senses.definitionCN: 使某地住满居民的行为，现多由相关动词表达
senses.example: The population of the frontier took three generations.
senses.exampleCN: 边疆的移民定居用了三代人的时间。
senses.why: The suffix -ation can name an action as well as a result. This older sense survives in the verb populate and in historical writing.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ation 既能命名结果，也能命名动作。这个较旧的义项保留在动词 populate 与历史写作中。

senses.title: A demographic problem
senses.titleCN: 人口结构：政策讨论里的对象
senses.definition: the size and age structure of a society considered as an economic or political issue
senses.definitionCN: 把社会的规模与年龄结构当作经济或政治问题来看待
senses.example: An ageing population puts pressure on pensions and hospitals.
senses.exampleCN: 人口老龄化给养老金和医院带来压力。
senses.why: Once governments began counting citizens for policy, population became a problem to be managed, not just a fact to be reported.
senses.whyCN: 当政府开始为政策清点公民，population 就从“被报告的事实”变成“待管理的问题”。

intro.en: Population comes from Latin populus 'the people' through populatio 'a peopling, a laying waste'. The word entered English in the 16th century on the Latin stem populatio(n-).
intro.cn: population 经由拉丁语 populatio“使人居住；蹂躏”上溯到 populus“人民”。16 世纪以拉丁词干 populatio(n-) 进入英语。

items.en: populus meant 'the people' as a body. Its deeper origin is uncertain; it may come from Etruscan, and no reliable Latin root can be given, so the deeper layer should be marked as uncertain in origin.
items.cn: populus 指作为整体的“人民”。其更深来源不确定，可能来自伊特鲁里亚语，无法给出可靠的拉丁词根，因此更深一层应标注“来源不确定”。

items.en: populatio in classical Latin could mean both 'a peopling, settlement' and 'a devastating, laying waste'. The two senses seem to come from two verbs that looked alike.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语中 populatio 既可指“使人定居”，也可指“蹂躏、毁坏”。两个义项似乎来自两个外形相近的动词。

items.en: English takes the word in the 1500s first as 'the peopling of a place', then quickly as 'the number of inhabitants'.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪先取“使地方有人居住”之义，随后很快转为“居民数量”。

items.en: With the growth of censuses in the 18th and 19th centuries, population becomes the standard word for an official count of residents.
items.cn: 18 至 19 世纪人口普查兴起，population 成为官方居民统计的标准用词。

items.en: In the 20th century biology adopts the word for any interbreeding group, transferring the census idea from citizens to individuals of one species.
items.cn: 20 世纪生物学借用该词指任何能相互繁殖的群体，把人口普查的思路从公民转到同一物种的个体。

items.en: Statistics completes the abstraction: the population is now any complete set from which a sample is drawn.
items.cn: 统计学完成了抽象化：population 现在指任何被抽样的完整集合。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the popul- shape and the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group shares the idea of people or counted individuals but differs in what is being counted.
note.cn: 形近组共享 popul- 外形与同一拉丁词干；近义组都涉及“人”或“被计数的个体”，差别在计数对象。

entries.definition: full of people, densely inhabited. It describes a place, while population names the people or their number.
entries.definitionCN: 人口稠密的；住满人的。它描述地方，而 population 命名人或其数量。

entries.definition: to fill an area with people or animals. It names the act that produces a population.
entries.definitionCN: 居住于；使有人居住。它命名产生 population 的那个动作。

entries.definition: liked by many people. It goes back to populus too, but through the sense 'of the people', not through counting them.
entries.definitionCN: 受欢迎的。它同样上溯到 populus，但走的是“属于人民的”这条义线，而不是计数。

entries.definition: the people who live in a place. It names them directly, while population can mean either the people or their count.
entries.definitionCN: 居民。它直接命名人，而 population 既可指人也可指数量。

entries.definition: people with legal membership in a state. It is a legal category, while population is a demographic count that includes non-citizens.
entries.definitionCN: 公民。它是法律范畴，而 population 是包含非公民的人口统计。

entries.definition: a group linked by shared place or interests. It stresses relationships, while population stresses mere co-presence and number.
entries.definitionCN: 社区；群体。它强调关系，而 population 强调共同在场与数量。

entries.definition: the statistical structure of a population, such as age and income. It analyses a population rather than naming it.
entries.definitionCN: 人口结构。指年龄、收入等统计构成，是对 population 的分析而非命名。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: popul- is the stem of Latin populus 'people', so population and popular sit in the same family.
normal.cn: popul- 是拉丁 populus“人民”的词干，所以 population 与 popular 同属一族。

normal.en: The -ation suffix turns people into a countable quantity, which is why the word collocates with growth, density and decline.
normal.cn: -ation 后缀把“人”变成可计量的量，所以这个词常与增长、密度、下降搭配。

normal.en: population density is arithmetic made visible: people divided by area.
normal.cn: 人口密度就是可视化的算术：人数除以面积。

normal.en: In biology the census frame is kept but the citizens become finches, wolves or trees.
normal.cn: 生物学保留了普查的计数框，只把公民换成了雀鸟、狼或树木。

normal.en: In statistics population is the whole set, and sample is the part taken from it.
normal.cn: 统计学里总体是全集，样本是从中取出的部分。

abstract.en: Picture a map covered with dots, then zoom in until each dot becomes a face.
abstract.cn: 想象一张布满小点的地图，再放大到每个点变成一张脸。

abstract.en: Picture a census form that asks one question only: how many of you are there?
abstract.cn: 想象一张只问一个问题的普查表：你们有多少人？

abstract.en: Picture a jar of seeds: the jar is the statistical population, the handful you test is the sample.
abstract.cn: 想象一罐种子：罐子是统计总体，抓出来试的一把是样本。

examples.en: Population growth slowed once the factories closed.
examples.cn: 工厂关闭后，人口增长放缓了。

examples.en: The study tracked a population of six hundred patients over five years.
examples.cn: 该研究在五年间追踪了六百名患者组成的人群。

examples.en: Statisticians distinguish the population from the sample drawn out of it.
examples.cn: 统计学家把总体与从中抽取的样本区别开来。

root: 拉丁 populus“人民”（更深来源不确定，可能出自伊特鲁里亚语）；populatio(n-) 词干 + -ation 名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all answer one question with different boundaries: how many are inside this frame?
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在回答同一个问题，只是换边界：这个框里有多少？

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a map of dots, each dot a person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张由小点构成的地图，每个点是一个人。

branches.en: COUNT AND BODY: the number and the living community are one word seen twice, once as arithmetic and once as society.
branches.cn: 数字与群体：数量与活生生的社区是同一个词的两种看法，一是算术，一是社会。

branches.en: NAMED SUBGROUP: students, patients and workers each get their own population once a boundary is drawn.
branches.cn: 特定人群：一旦画出边界，学生、病人、劳动者各自成一个人群。

branches.en: NON-HUMAN COUNT: breeding groups and wildlife numbers apply the census frame to other species.
branches.cn: 非人类计数：繁殖群体与野生动物数量把普查的框套到其他物种上。

branches.en: STATISTICAL WHOLE: the population is whatever complete set a sample is taken from.
branches.cn: 统计总体：population 就是任何被抽样的完整集合。

branches.en: PROCESS AND POLICY: settling an area and managing an ageing society are the verb side and the political side of the same noun.
branches.cn: 过程与政策：让人定居与管理老龄化社会，是同一名词的动词面与政治面。

intro.en: Population is the Latin stem popul- plus -ation. The suffix marks a result or an action, and the same stem yields the adjective populous and the verb populate.
intro.cn: population 是拉丁词干 popul- 加 -ation。后缀标记结果或动作，同一词干还产出形容词 populous 与动词 populate。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family runs from populus 'people' to populatio 'settlement, devastation' and populosus 'full of people'. English keeps popul- throughout.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族从 populus“人民”延伸到 populatio“定居、毁坏”与 populosus“人多的”。英语始终保留 popul-。

items.meaning: to fill a place with inhabitants
items.meaningCN: 居住于；使有人居住（popul-“人民”+ -ate 动词后缀）

items.meaning: the people of an area or a counted group

items.example: The population is estimated at two million.
It is the most populous province in the country.

latinEntries.meaningCN: 人民；国民（更深来源不确定）

definition_zh: 位置；方位；姿势；职位；立场；处境；安置；使处于
definition_en: the place where someone or something is, the way the body is arranged, a job, an opinion on an issue, a situation, or to put something in a particular place
core_image: 棋盘上一枚棋子被手指捏起，轻轻放进一个新的格子
scene: 比赛暂停时，教练把几枚棋子从棋盘边角挪到中央，又退后看了看。He moved the knight into a stronger position on the board.
sceneCN: 这里 position 是「位置」（第 1 个义项：某物所在的地方）；句意为他把马挪到棋盘上更有利的位置。图中可辨识物件：棋盘、棋子、教练。

pos.zh: 位置；方位；姿势；职位；立场；处境

derivatives.zh: 由 position 加 -al 构成，义为「位置的；与位置有关的」
由 position 加 -ing 构成，义为「定位；摆放」
由 position 加 -er 构成，义为「定位器；定位装置」

senses.title: The place where something is
senses.definition: the exact place where a person or thing is or should be
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物所在或应在的确切地点
senses.example: The map marks the position of every well in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 地图标出了山谷里每一口井的位置。
senses.why: Latin ponere means to place, and positio is a placing; the first sense is the result of that act, the spot where something has been put.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ponere 意为放置，positio 是「放置」这一动作；第一个义项就是动作的结果——某物被放定的那个点。

senses.title: The way the body is held
senses.definition: the way someone stands, sits or holds the body
senses.definitionCN: 人站立、坐着或摆放身体的方式
senses.example: Sit in a comfortable position with your back straight.
senses.exampleCN: 挺直背，以一种舒服的姿势坐好。
senses.why: A body placed this way or that forms a visible arrangement, so the placing word comes to name the shape the body makes.
senses.whyCN: 身体这样摆或那样摆，会形成看得见的安排；于是「放置」这个词开始指身体摆出的形状。

senses.title: A job or official role
senses.definition: a job in an organization, or the rank someone holds
senses.definitionCN: 在一个组织中的工作，或某人所居的级别
senses.example: She applied for a position in the research department.
senses.exampleCN: 她申请了研究部的一个职位。
senses.why: A post is a place in an ordered structure: the person is placed in it, and the word for the placing becomes the word for the slot.
senses.whyCN: 职位是有序结构中的一个位置：人被放进这个位置，于是表示「放置」的词变成了表示「位置、空缺」的词。

senses.title: An opinion on an issue
senses.definition: the opinion someone takes on a question, especially one they are prepared to defend
senses.definitionCN: 某人对某个问题所持的看法，尤指愿意为之辩护的看法
senses.example: The committee took a firm position against the new road.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会坚决反对修建这条新路。
senses.why: A standpoint is a place one stands; taking a position is choosing where to stand in an argument, so spatial placing turns into opinion.
senses.whyCN: 立场就是站的地方；表明立场就是在争论中选定站处，于是空间上的「放置」变成了看法。

senses.title: To put something in place
senses.definition: to put someone or something in a particular place or arrangement, often carefully
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物放到特定地点或安排中，往往带有仔细的意味
senses.example: He positioned the lamp so that the light fell on the page.
senses.exampleCN: 他把灯安置好，让光落在书页上。
senses.why: The noun names the resulting place; the verb is the act of producing it, and English formed the verb from the noun in modern times.
senses.whyCN: 名词指放置之后形成的位置；动词则是产生这个位置的动作，英语到近代才由名词造出这个动词。

intro.en: Position is the Latin verb ponere, to place, turned into a noun through its participle positus; English took it from French and later made a verb of it again.
intro.cn: position 是拉丁动词 ponere（放置）经其过去分词 positus 变成的名词；英语从法语借入，后来又把名词重新做成动词。

items.en: Ponere meant to put or place, and its past participle positus meant placed or set.
items.cn: ponere 意为放置、安放，它的过去分词 positus 意为被放置的。

items.en: Positio was the abstract noun for a placing, and it could already mean the place a thing occupied.
items.cn: positio 是表示「放置」的抽象名词，当时已经可以指某物占据的位置。

items.en: Old French passed position to English in the fourteenth century as a word for a place or an arrangement.
items.cn: 古法语在十四世纪把 position 传给英语，指位置或安排方式。

items.en: The word gained the senses of a military post, a job and a stated opinion, all built on the idea of a place one occupies.
items.cn: 这个词陆续获得军事据点、职位与明确看法等义项，全部建立在「所占之处」这一想法上。

items.en: Modern English formed the verb to position and added phrases such as market position, keeping the old placing core.
items.cn: 现代英语造出动词 to position，并添上 market position 一类说法，保留的仍是古老的「放置」核心。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin verb ponere; the near-meaning group gathers words for place, stance and job.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁动词 ponere 构成的词；近义组收表示地点、立场与职位的词。

entries.definition: Relating to position or place.
entries.definitionCN: 由 position 加 -al 构成，义为「位置的；与位置有关的」。

entries.definition: From Latin positivus and positus; it first meant placed or fixed, and now means affirmative.
entries.definitionCN: 与 positus 同根，原指被放置、被定下的，现代义为「肯定的」。

entries.definition: To put together, from com- plus ponere.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com-（一起）与 ponere（放置）构成，义为「组成；创作」。

entries.definition: To put down, from de- plus ponere.
entries.definitionCN: 由 de-（向下）与 ponere（放置）构成，义为「存放；沉积」。

entries.definition: The place where something is.
entries.definitionCN: 位置；地点；强调地理上的所在，不指姿势或立场。

entries.definition: A public attitude towards an issue, or the way the body stands.
entries.definitionCN: 立场；站姿；同时覆盖态度与身体姿态。

entries.definition: A job or a place where someone is stationed.
entries.definitionCN: 职位；岗位；强调被派驻的工作地点。

entries.definition: The act of putting something in a place, or a job arranged for someone.
entries.definitionCN: 安置；安排；强调安排的动作或实习岗位。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on the Latin verb for placing, and its family keeps returning to spots, postures, posts and stands.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词立足于拉丁语表示「放置」的动词，同族词反复回到地点、姿势、职位与立场。

normal.en: Ponere means to place, and its participle positus is the stem behind position, positive and posit.
normal.cn: ponere 意为放置，它的过去分词 positus 正是 position、positive 与 posit 共同的词干。

normal.en: Compose is com- plus ponere, to put together; deposit is de- plus ponere, to put down.
normal.cn: compose 是 com- 加 ponere，意为放在一起；deposit 是 de- 加 ponere，意为放下。

normal.en: Positional adds -al and simply describes anything about place or arrangement.
normal.cn: positional 加 -al，只用来描述与位置或安排有关的事物。

normal.en: A job is a position because a person is placed into a slot in an organization.
normal.cn: 职位之所以叫 position，是因为人被放进组织中的一个格子里。

normal.en: A position in an argument is a place to stand, which is why one word covers location and opinion.
normal.cn: 争论中的立场就是站的地方，所以一个词同时覆盖位置与看法。

abstract.en: A position is where you are, but also where you choose to stand, and English lets one word hold both.
abstract.cn: 位置既是你所在之处，也是你选择站立之处，英语让一个词同时装下两者。

abstract.en: On a board every piece has a position, and changing it changes what the piece can do.
abstract.cn: 棋盘上每枚棋子都有位置，改变位置就改变了它所能做的事。

abstract.en: To be in position is to be ready, which is why the word appears in sports, jobs and arguments alike.
abstract.cn: 就位就是准备好了，所以这个词在体育、职场与争论里都会出现。

examples.en: He moved the knight into a stronger position on the board.
examples.cn: 他把马挪到棋盘上更有利的位置。

examples.en: She applied for a position in the research department.
examples.cn: 她申请了研究部的一个职位。

examples.en: The committee took a firm position against the new road.
examples.cn: 委员会坚决反对修建这条新路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「坡贼神」——把棋子摆到棋盘上的某一点，那个点就定了；position 就是位置，也是职位与立场。

root: 源自拉丁 ponere（放置）的过去分词 positus，再由抽象名词 positio 经古法语进入英语；同族词有 compose、deposit、positive。注意与来自 portare（搬运）的 port、portable 区分：position 的核心是「放」，不是「搬」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a place something occupies; the senses branch into physical location, body posture, a job slot, a standpoint, and the act of placing.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是某物所占据的地方；义项由此分出物理位置、身体姿势、职位空缺、立场，以及放置的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chess piece lifted between two fingers and set down in a new square.
core.cn: 核心意象：棋盘上一枚棋子被手指捏起，轻轻放进一个新的格子。

branches.en: a marker pinned to a spot on a map
branches.cn: 钉在地图某点上的标记

branches.en: a back held straight in a chair
branches.cn: 椅子上挺直的背

branches.en: a name written into an empty slot on an org chart
branches.cn: 组织架构图空格里写下的名字

branches.en: a delegate standing to state a view
branches.cn: 代表站起来陈述看法

branches.en: a camera positioned to catch the whole stage
branches.cn: 被安放好以拍到整个舞台的相机

intro.en: The word is built from the Latin verb for placing, its participle and an action suffix, and the same pieces also build compose and deposit.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语「放置」动词、它的过去分词与一个动作名词后缀构成，同样的部件还造出了 compose 与 deposit。

latinIntro.en: Position comes from Latin ponere, to place, through its participle positus and the noun positio; the same verb also gives compose and deposit.
latinIntro.cn: position 来自拉丁 ponere（放置），经由过去分词 positus 与名词 positio；同一个动词还给出 compose 与 deposit。

items.meaning: forming nouns of action or result
com- plus ponere, to put together
items.meaningCN: 由 com- 与 ponere 构成，意为放在一起

items.meaning: de- plus ponere, to put down
items.meaningCN: 由 de- 与 ponere 构成，意为放下

definition_zh: 可能的；能做到的；很可能的；合适的；尽可能好的
definition_en: able to be done or to happen; likely but not certain; suitable in the circumstances
core_image: 一扇没有上锁的门：门后有路，但还没有人迈出去
scene: 面试结束后，年轻人站在公司门口，反复回想自己还有没有机会。The recruiter said a second interview was possible if the first one went well.
sceneCN: 这里是「有可能的」（第 1 个义项：事情能够发生）；句意为招聘人员说，如果初面顺利，二面是有可能的。画面里可留意的是那扇半开的门和候选人握着的手。

pos.zh: 可能的；能做到的；很可能的；合适的

derivatives.zh: possible 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，指「可能性」，-ity 把形容词变成抽象名词
possible 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，表示「也许；可能地」
否定前缀 im- 加 possible 构成，表示「不可能的」

senses.title: Able to be done or achieved
senses.definition: able to happen or be done, because nothing stands in the way
senses.definitionCN: 因为不存在阻碍，所以能够发生或做到
senses.example: A cure for the disease may be possible within ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 十年之内或许有可能找到这种病的疗法。
senses.why: The Latin verb posse means to be able; the first sense is bare ability with no obstacle in front of it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 posse 意为「能够」，所以这个词最初的义项就是「有能力、又没阻碍」。

senses.title: Likely to be true or to happen
senses.definition: having a strong chance of being true or of happening, though not certain
senses.definitionCN: 成真或发生的几率很大，但并不确定
senses.example: It is possible that the train will be late again.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟火车很可能再次晚点。
senses.why: Once a thing can happen, the same word is used for what a speaker judges will probably happen, so ability shades into likelihood.
senses.whyCN: 一件事既然能够发生，说话人就用同一个词来表达自己判断「大概会发生」，于是「能力」之外又添了「几率」。

senses.title: Suitable in a particular situation
senses.definition: acceptable or suitable for a purpose or a person, given the limits of the situation
senses.definitionCN: 在特定情境的限制下，对某个目的或某个人来说是合适、可接受的
senses.example: She is the only possible candidate for the job.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这份工作唯一合适的人选。
senses.why: If something can be done, it can also be chosen; the word then judges fitness instead of bare ability.
senses.whyCN: 一件事只要做得到，就可以被选中，于是这个词从「能不能」转为评判「合不合适」。

senses.title: As good as the situation allows
senses.definition: used after a superlative or with all, meaning the best that the circumstances permit
senses.definitionCN: 用于最高级之后或与 all 连用，表示在现有条件下能达到的最好程度
senses.example: We gave the visitors the best possible welcome.
senses.exampleCN: 我们给了来访者尽可能好的接待。
senses.why: When ability is stretched to its limit, possible stops meaning merely can and starts marking the ceiling of what can be reached.
senses.whyCN: 当「能够」被推到极限，possible 就不再只是「可以」，而是标出「能达到的上限」。

intro.en: Possible comes from Latin posse, to be able, whose stem joins an old word for power with the verb to be.
intro.cn: possible 出自拉丁语 posse（能够），其词干由表示「有力量」的古老词与动词「是」组合而成。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning powerful or able, usually written *poti-, is generally thought to lie behind the Latin family.
items.cn: 一般认为，表示「有力量、有能力」的重构词根 *poti- 是拉丁这一族词的远祖。

items.en: Latin potis meant able, capable or powerful, and it combined with esse, to be, to build the verb of ability.
items.cn: 拉丁语 potis 意为「有能力的、有力量的」，它与 esse（是）结合，构成表示「能够」的动词。

items.en: From posse Latin formed the adjective possibilis, meaning that which can be done or can exist.
items.cn: 拉丁语由 posse 造出形容词 possibilis，意为「做得到的、能够存在的」。

items.en: Old French took the adjective as possible and passed it to English, keeping the sense of what can be or can happen.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词写作 possible 并传入英语，保留了「能够存在或发生」的意思。

items.en: English added -ity for the abstract noun, -ly for the adverb and im- for the negative, so one Latin stem now covers a small family.
items.cn: 英语后来加上 -ity 构成抽象名词、加 -ly 构成副词、加 im- 构成否定式，同一个拉丁词干如今撑起了一个小词族。

note.en: The first group collects words built on the same Latin verb of ability; the second collects words that also talk about what may happen.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「能够」词族上的词；近义组收同样谈论「也许会发生」的词。

entries.definition: The adverb built from possible with -ly, meaning perhaps.
entries.definitionCN: 由 possible 加 -ly 构成的副词，意为「也许」。

entries.definition: Not able to happen or be done, formed with the negative prefix im-.
entries.definitionCN: 加否定前缀 im- 构成，意为「不可能的」。

entries.definition: The noun for the chance that something may exist or happen.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某事存在或发生的「可能性」的名词。

entries.definition: Powerful or effective, from the same old word for able that feeds posse.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「强有力的」，与 posse 同出表示「有能力」的古老词。

entries.definition: Expected to happen or probably true.
entries.definitionCN: 预期会发生或大概是真的。

entries.definition: Strongly likely, more confident than merely possible.
entries.definitionCN: 很有可能，语气比 possible 更确定。

entries.definition: Able to be carried out in practice, with the means available.
entries.definitionCN: 在现有条件下能够实际做到的。

entries.definition: Able to be imagined or believed, however unlikely.
entries.definitionCN: 能够被想象或相信的，尽管可能性很小。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb of ability, and its family keeps adding endings that turn ability into a noun, an adverb or its opposite.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「能够」的动词上，同族词不断加后缀，把「能力」变成名词、副词或它的反面。

normal.en: Posse in Latin means to be able, so anything possible is something you are able to do.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 posse 意为「能够」，所以 possible 就是「做得到的事」。

normal.en: Potis, the old word for able, also hides inside potent and potential, so power runs through the whole family.
normal.cn: 表示「有能力」的古词 potis 也藏在 potent 与 potential 里，力量贯穿整个词族。

normal.en: Add -ity to possible and the chance itself becomes a noun: possibility.
normal.cn: 在 possible 后加 -ity，机会本身就变成名词 possibility。

normal.en: Add im- to possible and the ability disappears: impossible.
normal.cn: 在 possible 前加 im-，能力就消失，成了 impossible。

normal.en: The phrase as soon as possible keeps the old sense of ability pressed against a deadline.
normal.cn: 短语 as soon as possible 把古老的「能力」之意压到一个截止时间上。

abstract.en: A door that is not locked is possible; whether anyone walks through it is a separate question.
abstract.cn: 门没上锁，这叫 possible；有没有人走进去，是另一回事。

abstract.en: Possible marks the edge of the map rather than a road already travelled.
abstract.cn: possible 标的是地图的边缘，而不是已经走过的路。

abstract.en: Every finished thing was once only possible, which is why the word keeps a hint of the future.
abstract.cn: 每件完成的事当初都只是 possible，所以这个词总带着一点未来的气味。

examples.en: Is it possible to finish the report by Friday?
examples.cn: 有可能在周五前完成报告吗？

examples.en: The doctors did everything possible to save him.
examples.cn: 医生们为救他做了一切能做的事。

examples.en: A peaceful solution is still possible.
examples.cn: 和平解决仍然是有可能的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕谁保」——怕谁保不住，事情就只好说「有可能」；记住 possible 表示可能的。

root: 拉丁语 posse（能够）← potis（有能力的）+ esse（是）；同族词多与「能力、可能」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is ability without obstruction; from there the word spreads to likelihood, to fitness for a purpose, and to the upper limit of what can be reached.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「有能力、无阻碍」；由此分出「可能性大小」「是否合适」，以及「能达到的上限」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door left unlocked, with a path visible behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇没有上锁的门，门后能看见一条路。

branches.en: a locked door that someone finally opens
branches.cn: 一扇终于被人打开的锁着的门

branches.en: a forecast that says rain is likely by evening
branches.cn: 预报说傍晚大概有雨

branches.en: a shortlist with only one suitable name on it
branches.cn: 名单上只剩一个合适的人

branches.en: a welcome pushed to its warmest
branches.cn: 把欢迎做到最热烈

branches.en: a seed that may or may not sprout
branches.cn: 一粒可能发芽也可能不发芽的种子

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin verb of ability, its older root of power, a suffix of possibility, and English endings that reverse or redirect it.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语「能够」动词、更早的「力量」词根、表示「可……的」后缀，以及英语中表示否定与副词的后缀共同构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin posse, potis and possibilis supply the core; the English family grows by prefix and suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的 posse、potis、possibilis 提供核心，英语这一族靠前缀与后缀继续生长。

definition_zh: 也许；可能地；（与 can、could 连用）究竟；能否
definition_en: perhaps; used with can or could to stress surprise or doubt, or to make a request sound polite
core_image: 一盏忽明忽暗的灯：会不会亮，此刻还说不准
scene: 朋友问周末要不要去爬山，她看了看窗外的乌云，没有马上答应。The sky may possibly clear up by Saturday morning.
sceneCN: 这里是「也许」（第 1 个义项：表示不确定）；句意为到周六早上天色也许会放晴。画面可留意的是窗外压低的云和那盏还没开的灯。

pos.zh: 也许；可能地；（用于强调或委婉请求）

derivatives.zh: possibly 加否定前缀 im- 构成，表示「不可能地；难以想象地」
possibly 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，表示「可能的」
同一词族的名词形式，表示「可能性」

senses.title: Perhaps; it may be so
senses.definition: used to say that something may be true or may happen, but is not certain
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事也许是真的，或者也许会发生，但并不确定
senses.example: She will possibly arrive before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 她也许中午前会到。
senses.why: The adverb carries the adjective's sense of ability into a judgement the speaker will not fully commit to.
senses.whyCN: 副词把形容词「能够」的意思带进一句说话人不敢完全担保的判断里，说的就是「也许」。

senses.title: Used with can or could for emphasis
senses.definition: used after can or could to show surprise, doubt or strong feeling about whether something is possible
senses.definitionCN: 用在 can 或 could 之后，对某事是否可能表示惊讶、怀疑或强烈语气
senses.example: How could she possibly forget the keys again?
senses.exampleCN: 她怎么可能又把钥匙忘了？
senses.why: If ability is stressed to its limit, a neutral question turns into a challenge to belief.
senses.whyCN: 把「能力」强调到极限，原本中性的问句就变成了对「这怎么可能」的质疑。

senses.title: Used to make a polite request
senses.definition: used in questions such as could you possibly to make a request sound careful and polite
senses.definitionCN: 用于 could you possibly 这类问句，使请求显得客气、留有余地
senses.example: Could you possibly send me the file today?
senses.exampleCN: 您今天能不能把文件发给我？
senses.why: Asking whether someone even has the ability to help softens the demand and leaves an easy way to refuse.
senses.whyCN: 先问对方「有没有可能帮上」，请求就变软了，也给对方留了容易拒绝的余地。

intro.en: Possibly is the adverb of possible, and both go back to the Latin verb posse, to be able.
intro.cn: possibly 是 possible 的副词，两者都追溯到拉丁语动词 posse（能够）。

items.en: Potis, an old Latin adjective for able or powerful, combined with esse, to be, to yield the verb of ability.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词 potis 表示「有能力的、有力量的」，它与 esse（是）结合，产生了表示「能够」的动词。

items.en: Posse meant to be able, and from it Latin built possibilis, that which can be done.
items.cn: posse 意为「能够」，拉丁语由它造出 possibilis，即「做得到的」。

items.en: Old French used possible for what can be or can happen, and English borrowed the adjective in this form.
items.cn: 古法语用 possible 表示「能够存在或发生的」，英语以这个形式借入了形容词。

items.en: Middle English possible described what is within reach or within reason, close to its modern meaning.
items.cn: 中古英语的 possible 指「做得到、说得通」的事，与现代义已经很接近。

items.en: English added the adverb ending -ly to the adjective, giving possibly, which marks an unsure judgement rather than an ability.
items.cn: 英语给这个形容词加上副词词尾 -ly，造出 possibly，用来标记没有把握的判断，而不是单纯的能力。

note.en: The first group follows the same Latin stem through its adjective, negative and noun forms; the second follows the meaning of uncertainty.
note.cn: 形近组沿同一拉丁词干看它的形容词、否定式与名词形式；近义组则沿「不确定」这条意义线展开。

entries.definition: The adjective that possibly is built from, meaning able to be or happen.
entries.definitionCN: possibly 所由构成的形容词，意为「可能的」。

entries.definition: Not able to happen or be done, with the negative prefix im-.
entries.definitionCN: 加否定前缀 im-，意为「不可能的」。

entries.definition: The noun naming the chance that something may be or happen.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某事可能存在或发生的「可能性」的名词。

entries.definition: The negative adverb, used of things too difficult to imagine.
entries.definitionCN: 否定副词，用于难以想象地困难的事物。

entries.definition: A neutral word for maybe, common in careful speech.
entries.definitionCN: 中性的「也许」，在谨慎的表述中很常见。

entries.definition: A plainer, more conversational way to say perhaps.
entries.definitionCN: 更口语、更朴素的「也许」。

entries.definition: More likely than not, a stronger claim than possibly.
entries.definitionCN: 多半如此，语气比 possibly 更肯定。

entries.definition: In a way that can be imagined, however slight the chance.
entries.definitionCN: 在可以想象的范围内，不论机会多小。

normalIntro.en: The word is an adjective of ability turned into an adverb, so its endings carry most of its history.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由表示「能够」的形容词转为副词，它的历史大半写在词尾上。

normal.en: Possibly is possible plus -ly, the ordinary English way of turning an adjective into an adverb.
normal.cn: possibly 就是 possible 加 -ly，这是英语把形容词变成副词最普通的方式。

normal.en: The -ly ending adds no doubt of its own; the uncertainty already sits inside possible.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 本身并不带来怀疑，不确定早就藏在 possible 里。

normal.en: Impossibly adds im- to possibly and closes the door: not even able to be imagined.
normal.cn: impossibly 在 possibly 前加 im-，把门关死，意为「连想都不可能」。

normal.en: In could you possibly, the adverb stretches ability into politeness rather than doubt.
normal.cn: 在 could you possibly 里，这个副词把「能力」拉长成客气，而不是怀疑。

normal.en: The double s in the spelling marks the Latin stem pos-se, which also shows in possible and impossible.
normal.cn: 拼写里的双写 s 标出拉丁词干 pos-se，在 possible 与 impossible 里同样出现。

abstract.en: Possibly is the word for leaving a door ajar without promising to walk through it.
abstract.cn: possibly 是「把门留着缝，却不保证走进去」时用的词。

abstract.en: A forecast lives on possibly: it names a chance rather than a fact.
abstract.cn: 天气预报就活在 possibly 上：它给的是机会，不是事实。

abstract.en: Saying possibly moves the weight of proof away from the speaker and onto the future.
abstract.cn: 说 possibly，就把举证的分量从说话人身上推给了未来。

examples.en: The meeting will possibly be moved to Thursday.
examples.cn: 会议也许会被改到周四。

examples.en: Could you possibly lend me your notes?
examples.cn: 你能不能把笔记借给我？

examples.en: She is possibly the best player on the team.
examples.cn: 她也许是队里最好的球员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕谁不力」——怕谁不肯出力，事情就只能说「也许」；记住 possibly 表示可能地。

root: possibly 由 possible 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，词干回到拉丁语 posse（能够）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an unsure maybe; the same adverb then hardens into emphatic disbelief and softens into a polite request.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是不确定的「也许」；同一个副词既能加重成质疑，也能放软成客气的请求。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp that flickers, so nobody can say yet whether the room will be lit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏忽明忽暗的灯，房间会不会亮起来，此刻没人说得准。

branches.en: a forecast that keeps changing its mind
branches.cn: 一份反复改口的预报

branches.en: a friend asking how such a thing could ever happen
branches.cn: 朋友追问这种事怎么可能发生

branches.en: a carefully worded request left open to refusal
branches.cn: 一句留好退路的请求

branches.en: a rumour that nobody can confirm
branches.cn: 一则没人能证实的传闻

branches.en: a question mark placed before a favour
branches.cn: 在请求前放一个问号

intro.en: The word is an adjective of ability plus the English adverb ending, and its family adds a negative prefix and a noun suffix around the same Latin stem.
intro.cn: 这个词是「能够」的形容词加英语副词词尾构成，词族在同一拉丁词干周围再加否定前缀与名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin posse and possibilis carry the core meaning; the English adverb ending does the grammatical work.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的 posse 与 possibilis 承载核心意义，英语副词词尾负责语法功能。

definition_zh: 邮政；邮件；职位；柱子；邮寄；张贴；发布
definition_en: the mail service or the mail itself; a job; an upright pole; to send by mail or to put a message where people can see it
core_image: 一根木桩立在路边，桩上钉着一块写满消息的木板
scene: 村口的老木门上贴着一张寻物启事，路过的人都停下脚步看。Someone had posted a notice about a lost dog on the gate.
sceneCN: 这里是「张贴、发布」（第 5 个义项：把消息公开出来）；句意为有人在门上贴了一张寻狗启事。画面里可留意木桩、旧门和那张被风掀起的纸。

derivatives.zh: post 加表示费用的后缀 -age 构成，指「邮费」
post 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，表示「邮政的」
post（张贴）加 -er 构成，原指张贴的告示，现多指「海报」

senses.title: The mail service and the letters it carries
senses.definition: the system that collects and delivers letters and parcels, or those letters and parcels themselves
senses.definitionCN: 收寄并投递信件、包裹的系统，也指这些信件与包裹本身
senses.example: The cheque came by post this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 支票是今天上午邮寄到的。
senses.why: Post first named a relay station where horses were changed; the letters that travelled from station to station took the name, and then the whole service did.
senses.whyCN: post 最初指换马的驿站；一站一站传下去的信件借用了这个名称，最后整套邮政系统也沿用了它。

senses.title: A job or position in an organization
senses.definition: a job in an organization, especially one with a title and fixed duties
senses.definitionCN: 组织中的一个职位，尤指有头衔、职责固定者
senses.example: She applied for a post in the finance department.
senses.exampleCN: 她申请了财务部的一个职位。
senses.why: A post was also a place where a soldier or official was stationed, so the word slid from the spot to the duty held at that spot.
senses.whyCN: post 也指士兵或官员驻扎的地点，词义便从「那个位置」滑到「在那个位置上承担的职务」。

senses.title: An upright pole set in the ground
senses.definition: a strong upright piece of wood or metal fixed in the ground, used to support something or mark a boundary
senses.definitionCN: 固定在地里的坚固木柱或金属柱，用来支撑物件或标示界线
senses.example: A wooden post marks the end of the path.
senses.exampleCN: 一根木桩标出了小路的尽头。
senses.why: This is the oldest line of all: Latin postis named a doorpost or upright beam, and English kept the solid object.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一条线：拉丁语 postis 指门柱或直立的梁木，英语保留了这件实物本身。

senses.title: To send a letter or parcel by mail
senses.definition: to send a letter, parcel or message through the postal system
senses.definitionCN: 通过邮政系统寄出信件、包裹或消息
senses.example: I posted the documents to the embassy yesterday.
senses.exampleCN: 我昨天把文件寄给了大使馆。
senses.why: Once post named the mail service, the noun turned into a verb: to post something is to hand it over to that service.
senses.whyCN: post 既然指邮政系统，名词就顺势转为动词，表示「把东西交给这套系统」。

senses.title: To put a notice or message where people can see it
senses.definition: to put up a notice in public, or to publish a message, picture or piece of writing online
senses.definitionCN: 把通知张贴在公共处，或在网上发布消息、图片、文字
senses.example: The school posted the exam results on its website.
senses.exampleCN: 学校把考试成绩发布在网站上。
senses.why: A post is a fixed place; to post something was to fix it there for everyone to read, and the internet reused the same picture for a screen.
senses.whyCN: post 是一个固定的位置；把东西 post 出来就是把它固定在那里让人人可读，网络时代把这幅画面搬到了屏幕上。

intro.en: Two Latin lines meet in this short word: postis, an upright beam, and posta, a station on a road, which itself comes from ponere, to place.
intro.cn: 两条拉丁线索在这个短词里汇合：postis 是直立的梁柱，posta 是路上的驿站，而 posta 又出自 ponere（放置）。

items.en: Postis meant a doorpost or upright beam, and this line alone gives English the wooden pole.
items.cn: postis 意为门柱或直立的梁木，仅这一条线就给了英语「木柱」这个义项。

items.en: The mail line starts elsewhere: ponere meant to put or place, and its participle positus, placed, stands behind the later station word.
items.cn: 邮政那条线另有起点：ponere 意为放置，它的过去分词 positus（被放置的）是后来「驿站」一词的背后形式。

items.en: Posta named a station on a road where horses and messengers were changed, a place where things were set down.
items.cn: posta 指路上换马、换信使的站点，也就是把人和物「安置下来」的地方。

items.en: English borrowed the French form poste for the riders and the letters, so post came to mean the mail and the office that handled it.
items.cn: 英语借入法语形式 poste，指骑马送信的人和信件，于是 post 兼指邮件与经办邮件的机构。

items.en: Modern English keeps both lines apart: the beam stays a post, while the station line grows into job posts, posting a letter and posting online.
items.cn: 现代英语把两条线分开保留：梁柱仍是 post，而「驿站」一线则长出职位、寄信与网络发布。

note.en: The first group collects words built on post with different endings; the second collects words for mail, for jobs and for poles, the three fields this word covers.
note.cn: 形近组收在 post 上加不同词尾构成的词；近义组收邮件、职位、柱子这三片词义场里的词。

entries.definition: The charge for sending mail, built with the suffix -age.
entries.definitionCN: 加后缀 -age 构成，指寄邮件所需的「邮费」。

entries.definition: Relating to the mail service, built with -al.
entries.definitionCN: 加后缀 -al 构成，表示「邮政的」。

entries.definition: A printed sheet put up for people to see, from the verb post.
entries.definitionCN: 由动词 post 而来，指张贴出来供人观看的印刷品「海报」。

entries.definition: A card sent by mail without an envelope.
entries.definitionCN: 不装信封、直接邮寄的「明信片」。

entries.definition: Letters and parcels, or the system that carries them.
entries.definitionCN: 信件与包裹，或运送它们的系统。

entries.definition: A job or rank held in an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 在组织中担任的职务或职位。

entries.definition: A tall upright support, often of stone.
entries.definitionCN: 高而直立的支撑物，常为石制。

entries.definition: To make writing or information available to the public.
entries.definitionCN: 把文字或信息公之于众。

normalIntro.en: Two Latin sources feed one spelling, and the senses sort themselves by which source they come from.
normalIntro.cn: 两条拉丁来源喂给同一个拼写，各个义项按来源自然分成两堆。

normal.en: The mail sense grows from posta, a relay station; letters moved from station to station along the road.
normal.cn: 邮政义出自 posta（驿站）；信件沿着大路一站一站往前传。

normal.en: The pole sense grows from postis, a doorpost, and has nothing to do with mail.
normal.cn: 柱子义出自 postis（门柱），与邮件毫无关系。

normal.en: Postage and postal keep the mail line, both built on post with different suffixes.
normal.cn: postage 与 postal 都留在邮政这条线上，只是加了不同后缀。

normal.en: A poster was first something posted up for people to read, before it meant a printed picture.
normal.cn: poster 最初指「张贴出来供人阅读的东西」，后来才指印刷的海报。

normal.en: To post a comment online repeats the old act of fixing a notice where others can see it.
normal.cn: 在网上 post 一条评论，重复的正是把告示固定在人人都看得见的地方。

abstract.en: One short word holds a wooden pole and a worldwide mail service because both are things set in a fixed place.
abstract.cn: 一个短词同时装着一根木桩和一套全球邮政，因为两者都是「被安置在固定位置」的东西。

abstract.en: A job post is a station for a person, just as a post was a station for a horse.
abstract.cn: 职位是人驻守的站点，正如当年的驿站是马匹换乘的站点。

abstract.en: Posting online is the village notice board moved onto a screen.
abstract.cn: 网络发布就是把村口的告示板搬到了屏幕上。

examples.en: Please post the letter before noon.
examples.cn: 请在中午前把信寄出去。

examples.en: He has held the post of manager for five years.
examples.cn: 他担任经理一职已经五年。

examples.en: A tall post supports the wire fence.
examples.cn: 一根高高的木桩撑着铁丝围栏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖斯特」——把邮包剖开再送出去；记住 post 既指邮寄，也指柱子。

root: 两条拉丁来源：postis（门柱、直立的梁木）给「柱子」；posta（驿站）及其背后的 ponere（放置）给「邮政、职位」。

sensesIntro.en: The pole is the older physical sense; the station line then yields mail, the job held at a place, and finally the act of making something public.
sensesIntro.cn: 「柱子」是更早的实物义；「驿站」一线则长出邮件、驻守的职位，最后长出「公之于众」的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden stake by the road with a message nailed to it.
core.cn: 核心意象：路边一根木桩，上面钉着一块写着消息的木板。

branches.en: a wooden stake holding up a fence
branches.cn: 木桩撑起一段栅栏

branches.en: a bag of letters moving from town to town
branches.cn: 一袋信件在城镇间传递

branches.en: a nameplate fixed on an office door
branches.cn: 固定在办公室门上的名牌

branches.en: a stamped envelope dropped into a box
branches.cn: 贴好邮票的信封投进邮筒

branches.en: a notice flapping on a gate
branches.cn: 门上被风吹动的告示

intro.en: Two Latin sources meet here: postis, an upright beam, and posta, a station on a road, itself from ponere, to place.
intro.cn: 这个词有两条拉丁来源：postis 是直立的梁柱，posta 是路上的驿站，而 posta 又出自 ponere（放置）。

latinIntro.en: The Latin nouns postis and posta, with the verb ponere behind the second, explain both the pole and the mail.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁名词 postis 与 posta 分别解释了「柱子」与「邮政」，后者背后还有动词 ponere。

definition_zh: 海报；招贴画；张贴者
definition_en: a large printed notice or picture put up in a public place; a person who posts letters or messages
core_image: 车站墙上贴着一张大海报，颜色鲜艳，路过的人都忍不住多看一眼
scene: 车站大厅的墙上新贴了一张电影宣传画。A colorful poster by the ticket office promised that the film would open next week.
sceneCN: 这里 poster 是「海报、招贴画」（第 1 个义项：贴在公共场所的大幅印刷品）；句意为售票处旁一张色彩鲜艳的海报预告电影下周上映。

pos.zh: 海报；招贴画；贴在墙上的大幅印刷品

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「邮政；柱子；（网络）帖子」，也是动词「张贴；邮寄」
由 post 加 -age 构成，义为「邮资」
由 poster 与 board 复合而成，义为「海报纸板」

senses.title: A large printed notice for public display
senses.definition: a large printed sheet of paper with a picture or announcement, put up where many people will see it
senses.definitionCN: 印着图画或告示的大幅印刷品，贴在很多人能看到的地方
senses.example: They put up posters to advertise the school concert.
senses.exampleCN: 他们贴出海报为学校音乐会做宣传。
senses.why: To post is to fix something where the public passes; a poster is simply the large sheet that gets posted.
senses.whyCN: post 作动词是把东西固定在公众来往之处，poster 就是那张被贴上去的大纸。

senses.title: A person who posts
senses.definition: a person who posts letters, notices or messages, now often someone who publishes content online
senses.definitionCN: 张贴信件、告示或发送消息的人，现在常指在网上发布内容的人
senses.example: The forum ranks its most active posters every month.
senses.exampleCN: 论坛每月给最活跃的发帖人排名。
senses.why: Adding -er to post names the doer of the action, so the word follows the person wherever posting happens, from a notice board to a forum.
senses.whyCN: post 加 -er 构成动作执行者，于是这个词跟着「张贴」这个动作走，从布告栏一直走到论坛。

intro.en: Poster is built on post, an English word with two Latin sources: the postal sense runs from ponere, the upright-stake sense from popularis, and the poster we hang came through the mailing sense.
intro.cn: poster 建立在 post 之上；post 有两个拉丁来源：邮政义来自 ponere（放置），立柱义来自 popularis，而海报义走的是邮寄这一路。

items.en: Latin ponere meant to place, to put; from it came pausare, to halt, and the idea of setting something down.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ponere 意为放置、安放，由此派生出 pausare（停驻），以及「把某物安放下来」的观念。

items.en: Medieval Latin postare gave post, first the fixed stations where mail was set down and changed horses, then the mail itself.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 postare 给出 post，先指放置邮件、换马的固定驿站，后指邮件本身。

items.en: Old French poste carried both the fixed station and the mail that moved between stations; it also named an upright stake, a separate Latin line from popularis.
items.cn: 古法语 poste 兼指固定驿站和往来其间的邮件；它还指立柱，那来自另一条拉丁语线索 popularis。

items.en: English post covered the mail, an upright stake, and the act of fixing a notice where the public passes.
items.cn: 英语的 post 兼指邮件、立柱，以及把告示固定在公众经过之处的动作。

items.en: From post came poster, first the person who posts, then the large printed sheet meant to be posted on walls; today it also names online content images.
items.cn: 由 post 派生出 poster，先指张贴者，后指专供张贴的大幅印刷品；如今也指网上的图片内容。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the post family and one word that only echoes the ending; the near-meaning group gathers printed things meant for the public eye.
note.cn: 形近组收 post 词族的词，另收一个只是词尾相像的词；近义组收面向公众的各类印刷品。

entries.definition: The mail, an upright stake, or the act of fixing a notice; the first element of poster.
entries.definitionCN: 邮件、立柱，或张贴告示的动作；poster 的基础词。

entries.definition: The charge for sending mail, built on post with the suffix -age.
entries.definitionCN: 邮寄费用；由 post 加后缀 -age 构成。

entries.definition: The act of posting a letter or publishing an online message.
entries.definitionCN: 投寄信件或发布网络消息的行为。

entries.definition: A list of names and duties; it echoes the -ster ending but has a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 值班名单；词尾与 poster 相像，来源不同。

entries.definition: A written or printed announcement put up for people to read.
entries.definitionCN: 张贴出来供人阅读的书面告示。

entries.definition: A printed notice or advertisement, especially one posted in public.
entries.definitionCN: 印刷的告示或广告，尤指贴在公共场所的。

entries.definition: A displayed board or notice giving information or directions.
entries.definitionCN: 提供信息或指引的展示牌、标牌。

normalIntro.en: Everything in the word points back to post: the sheet is made to be posted, and the person is the one who posts it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词的一切都回指 post：那张纸是为张贴而做的，那个人是执行张贴的人。

normal.en: Poster = post + er: first the doer, then the thing that gets done to, a sheet for posting.
normal.cn: poster = post + er：先指做动作的人，后指承受动作的东西，即供张贴的大纸。

normal.en: Post ultimately traces to Latin ponere, to place: a poster is simply a picture placed on public view.
normal.cn: post 最终可溯至拉丁语 ponere（放置）：海报就是被放到公众视野里的一幅画。

normal.en: To post a letter and to post a notice use the same word; a poster is the notice enlarged.
normal.cn: 寄信和张贴告示用的是同一个动词；海报就是放大了的告示。

normal.en: The plural is regular: poster becomes posters.
normal.cn: 复数规则变化：poster 变 posters。

normal.en: Online posters are the modern heirs: same word, new wall, the screen.
normal.cn: 网络发帖人是它的现代后裔：同一个词，换了一堵新墙——屏幕。

abstract.en: A poster is a wall speaking: it shouts one picture and five words to everyone passing.
abstract.cn: 海报是一面会说话的墙：向每个路过的人喊出一幅图和五个词。

abstract.en: Posters sell dreams at the height of the eye, exactly where you look while waiting.
abstract.cn: 海报在视线的高度出售梦想，恰好是你等候时会看的地方。

abstract.en: A city without posters is a room with nothing on its walls.
abstract.cn: 没有海报的城市，像一堵什么都不挂的墙围成的房间。

examples.en: They put up posters to advertise the school concert.
examples.cn: 他们贴出海报为学校音乐会做宣传。

examples.en: A colorful poster by the ticket office promised that the film would open next week.
examples.cn: 售票处旁一张色彩鲜艳的海报预告电影下周上映。

examples.en: He designed a poster for the sports meet and posted it near the gate.
examples.cn: 他为运动会设计了一张海报，贴在大门附近。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖斯特」——把海报「剖」开来「贴」上墙，路人都「特」别爱看，这就是 poster。

root: poster 由 post 加执行者后缀 -er 构成；post 经中世纪拉丁语 postare 与古法语 poste 进入英语，邮政义可溯至拉丁语 ponere（放置），立柱义另有来源 popularis，两条线索在古法语交汇。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a sheet fixed where the public passes; the senses run from the printed notice itself to the person who posts letters or messages.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是固定在公众必经之处的一张大纸；义项从印好的招贴本身，走到投寄信件、发布消息的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright sheet pasted on a station wall, read by everyone who waits.
core.cn: 核心意象：车站墙上一张鲜亮的纸，等车的人都看它。

branches.en: a film poster by the ticket office
branches.cn: 售票处的电影海报

branches.en: concert posters pasted across campus
branches.cn: 贴满校园的音乐会海报

branches.en: the worker posting bills on the hoarding
branches.cn: 往围板上贴告示的工人

branches.en: an active poster in an online forum
branches.cn: 论坛里活跃的发帖人

branches.en: posters calling for volunteers, posted and reposted

intro.en: The word is a plain English derivation, but its base post carries two Latin lines that met in Old French.
intro.cn: 这个词是简单的英语派生词，但它的基础词 post 带着两条在古法语交汇的拉丁线索。

latinIntro.en: The postal line runs through Medieval Latin postare from ponere; that chain is recorded and listed as the Latin entries.
latinIntro.cn: 邮政一条线经中世纪拉丁语 postare 上溯 ponere；这条链条有据可查，列为拉丁条目。
